The game then decides the order on its own, working left to right across the jobs (the leftmost enabled task is attempted first). Basic mode is perfectly fine for a new colony: you can leave it here, get comfortable with the rest of the game, and come back to manual priorities later.
  • Manual priority mode lets you set a number from 1 to 4 on each job, giving you direct control over the order. It is more work up front, but it is the only way to say "doctor first, haul only when there is nothing better to do." The docs assume manual mode once you are ready for it.

docs.title: Setting priorities in manual mode (focused view)
docs.text:
In manual mode, in the focused view, jobs are organized by priority level:

  • Up/Down move between priority levels (1 through 4, plus Disabled).
  • Left/Right move between jobs within the current priority level.
  • Tab/Shift+Tab move to the next or previous pawn.

You can also start typing a job's name to jump straight to it, wherever it currently sits. While a search is running, Up/Down step through the matches, and Enter or Shift+Enter settles on the one you are hearing without closing the menu.

To set a priority, press a number key:

  • 1 is the highest priority.
  • 2, 3, and 4 step down from there.
  • 0 turns the job off entirely.

Enter and Escape both save and close the tab.

As you arrow left and right through a priority level, the mod announces each job's name, skill level, passion, a description, and the specific sub-tasks it includes, in the order the pawn performs them. Some of those sub-tasks are spoken with an "E" in front. The "E" is a spoken marker, not a key you press: it flags a task the game treats as an emergency (such as firefighting or rescuing a downed colonist), which a pawn will drop other work to attend to.

docs.title: Bulk operations and bracket cycling
docs.text:
These keys work the same in both the focused view and the table view.

[ cycles the current job's priority up (lower number, more important). ] cycles it down (higher number, less important).

Add Shift to apply the same cycle to every eligible colonist at once: Shift+[ raises the priority for every pawn, Shift+] lowers it for every pawn.

Shift+number (0 through 4) sets that job to the chosen priority for every eligible colonist at once.

docs.title: Copying a colonist's priorities
docs.text:
Once one colonist's jobs are set the way you want them, you can hand the whole set to someone else. These keys work in the focused view and the table view alike, and they use the same clipboard as the copy and paste buttons a sighted player clicks.

  • Ctrl+C copies the priorities of the colonist you are on.
  • Ctrl+V pastes them onto the colonist you are on.

Paste needs a copy first, so pressing Ctrl+V before anything has been copied just says so. Jobs a colonist can never do are left alone.

docs.title: How execution order works
docs.text: The game runs all priority-1 jobs first, reading them left to right across the row, then all priority-2 jobs left to right, and so on down to 4. Two jobs at the same priority number resolve by their left-to-right position. This is why the order within a priority level matters alongside the number.

docs.title: Table view
docs.text:
The table view gives a colonist-per-row, job-per-column layout. The same concepts as the focused view apply, plus a set of painting tools that exist only here. All the standard table controls apply:

  • Up/Down move between colonists.
  • Left/Right move between jobs.
  • Alt+S sorts by the current column.
  • Shift+Up/Down paints the current cell's value onto rows above or below as you move.
  • Shift+Home/End paints from the current row to the top or bottom of the column.
  • Ctrl+Shift+Home/End paints the value across every row in the column at once.

Painting (the Shift+Up/Down and Shift+Home/End keys above) is available only in the table view. The bracket keys ([ / ] and their Shift variants) and Shift+number behave the same in both views.

See navigating menus for the full table grammar.

docs.title: The unskilled-job warning
docs.text: When you enable a job the pawn has no skill in, you will hear a warning sound. It is not blocking you, just a notice. Sometimes assigning unskilled work is exactly what you want (someone has to haul rocks). Other times it signals that you are about to let your best researcher attempt surgery.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text: Deciding which priorities to give which pawns is a strategy topic in its own right. The RimWorld wiki's Work page covers the trade-offs in depth.

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:
• The Schedule tab decides when pawns work; the Work tab decides what they do.
  • Checking on pawns shows a pawn's skills and passions, which is useful to have open while assigning work.

docs.title: Checking on pawns
docs.text:
Colonists (the game calls them pawns) need attention constantly: who is hurt, who is in a bad mood, who should be on the guns. This page covers how to get a fast read on any pawn from the map without opening a full screen.

For selecting pawns, cycling through colonists, and building combat groups, see selecting pawns.

docs.title: The at-a-glance info keys
docs.text:
These keys give a quick spoken summary of the pawn under the cursor, or the currently selected pawn if the cursor is not on a specific one.

  • Alt+H: quick health readout, focused on what matters in combat or triage: consciousness, movement, manipulation, and whether the pawn is bleeding. Use this to decide who needs immediate attention.
  • Alt+M: mood.
  • Alt+N: needs.
  • Alt+G: gear (what they are wielding and wearing).
  • Alt+K: top 3 skills.
  • Alt+B: the pawn's recent combat log (their last several fights).

These prioritize the thing under the cursor first, then fall back to the pawn you selected with comma/period or an Alt+number. Place the cursor on an enemy raider and press Alt+H to get the raider's health, not your selected colonist's. Move the cursor off anything specific and the keys report on the selected pawn instead.

docs.title: Finding conditions with type-ahead
docs.text:
For a deeper read on a pawn's health state, open the pawn's inspect view (press Enter on the pawn under the cursor, or Ctrl+Alt+Enter on a pawn selected via the colonist bar). From the top section of the inspect screen, start typing to jump to a condition:

  • "inf" jumps to infections.
  • "leg" or "arm" or "head" (or even "hea") jumps to everything wrong with that body part.

Arrow Up and Down through matching results. This is the fastest way to find a specific injury or condition without scrolling through the full list.

docs.title: The skills table (Alt+P)
docs.text:
To compare every colonist's skills side by side, press Alt+P to open the skills table. It lists all your colonists against all their skills.

Inside the table, Alt+S sorts by the column you are on, so you can jump to a skill column and find your strongest pawn for it. Press Alt+S again to flip the sort direction, and once more to clear it.

This pairs naturally with setting up work priorities: find your best cook in the skills table, then assign cooking to them.

docs.title: Where to go from here
docs.text: These keys assume you are on the colony map. For the basics of moving the cursor and camera, see the map. For a deeper read on a single pawn (full health detail, operations, traits, relationships), open the relevant tab via the inspect view. The at-a-glance keys above are for the constant spot-checks that keep a colony running.

docs.title: The context menu
docs.text:
Press ] (right bracket) to open the context menu. Arrow Up and Down through the options and press Enter to choose one. [ (left bracket) fires the top option immediately without opening the menu. Shift+[ queues the top option instead of doing it right away.

The context menu lists the actions available for the selected pawn at the cursor tile. It is the keyboard equivalent of a right-click menu. With a colonist selected, pressing ] on a tile or object shows what that colonist can do there. Point the cursor at a weapon on the ground, press ], and the menu might offer "Equip bolt-action rifle." Press Enter to issue the order.

The list changes with context. A pawn near a door, a downed colonist, or a stack of steel each produce different options. On a designation type in the Architect menu (such as a chop-wood order), the menu offers bulk actions like "Cancel all designations," which wipes every matching order at once.

docs.title: On the world map
docs.text: The context menu works the same way on the world map. Select a caravan with comma and period, move the cursor to a destination tile, and press ]. You get options such as "Travel to," "Trade with," or "Attack," depending on what is on that tile. The selected caravan is the actor and the cursor tile is the target, exactly as a selected pawn acts on a tile back home. For commanding the caravan itself (settle, split, rest, merge), use its gizmos with G.

docs.title: A DLC example: picking a xenotype (Biotech)
docs.text:
During character creation with the Biotech DLC active, the context menu is how you change a colonist's xenotype. Place the cursor on a pawn, press ], and the menu includes the pawn's current xenotype (usually "Baseliner"). Press Enter on it to open a list of every xenotype.

For more on pawns, see selecting pawns.

docs.title: Gizmos (the G key)
docs.text:
Gizmos are the contextual command buttons that appear when you select something: deconstruct a wall, reinstall a bed, form a caravan, rename a zone, and so on. Whatever is under the cursor, its gizmos are the actions available for it.

Press G with the cursor over an object to open its gizmo menu.

docs.title: Opening and using the menu
docs.text:
Place the cursor on an object (a building, furniture, a pawn, a caravan) and press G. The mod reads the gizmos available for that object. Arrow Up and Down to move through them and press Enter to activate the one you want.

What appears depends entirely on what is under the cursor. A wall offers deconstruct. A bed offers reinstall and deconstruct. A finished caravan hitching spot offers "Form caravan." If an object has no actions available, the menu will be short or empty.

docs.title: Gizmos with a target you can set
docs.text:
Some gizmos are sliders rather than buttons: the hemogen target on a bloodfeeder, the target fuel level on a generator, the psyfocus target on a psycaster, the suppression threshold on an entity. When one of these is focused in the menu, press Left and Right to move its target. Each press announces the new value and takes effect immediately, the same as dragging the bar with a mouse. Hold Shift for larger steps.

Enter on these gizmos still does whatever the gizmo's own button does: toggle whether hemogen packs are allowed, toggle auto refuel, toggle the neural heat limiter, toggle auto-suppression.

docs.title: Gizmos can carry their own shortcuts
docs.text:
As you arrow through the menu, the mod announces a gizmo's keyboard shortcut when it has one. These shortcuts come from the game, but RimWorld Access uses the plain letter keys for its own navigation. So it delegates a gizmo's shortcut to Shift plus that letter: if a gizmo's vanilla key is B, you press Shift+B to fire it.

You can trigger a gizmo this way without opening the menu at all. With the right object under the cursor, press Shift plus the gizmo's letter and the action runs immediately. Once you know an object's common shortcuts, you can skip the G menu.

docs.title: When two gizmos share a shortcut
docs.text: Sometimes two gizmos share the same shortcut. Pressing it opens a short menu of the choices: arrow to the one you want and press Enter. You pick from the menu rather than pressing the shortcut a second time.

docs.title: A worked example: moving a bed
docs.text:
1. Place the cursor on the bed.
  2. Press G to open its gizmos, arrow to "Reinstall," and press Enter. (Or press the reinstall gizmo's Shift+letter shortcut directly.)
  3. You are now in placement mode. Move the cursor to where you want the bed to go.
  4. Press Space to place it, then Enter to confirm.

Deconstruct works the same way: it is another gizmo in that same menu. For the full walkthrough of moving and removing things, see moving and reinstalling.

docs.title: Where gizmos appear
docs.text:
• On the colony map, gizmos command buildings, furniture, and pawns.
  • On the world map, gizmos command caravans: settle, split, rest, merge, and more.
  • During building placement, the gizmo menu is unavailable. You cannot open it until placement is finished.

When you have selected an object and want to know what you can do with it, press G.

docs.title: The info card (Alt+I)
docs.text:
The info card is the detailed stats screen for whatever the cursor touches. It exposes the numbers that drive the simulation: a terrain's fertility and movement cost, a wall's material and hit points, a pawn's full stat sheet, an item's value and quality.

Press Alt+I to open the info card for the thing under the cursor. Alongside G (gizmos) and ] (the context menu), it is one of the keys you reach for constantly.

docs.title: On the map
docs.text:
Point the cursor at almost anything and press Alt+I to open its info card: terrain, a pawn, a wall, an item. When a tile holds more than one thing, the mod opens a small menu so you can choose which one's card to read.

The card shines when you want numbers a quick readout won't give you. Making a growing zone? Press Alt+I on the available plants to compare their stats. Outfitting a colonist? Press it on a piece of clothing to see its protection and insulation. Press it on a colonist for their full stat sheet, or use Ctrl+Alt+I to open the info card of the pawn currently selected on the colonist bar, wherever your cursor happens to be.

docs.title: In other places
docs.text:
Alt+I appears on several screens beyond the map:

  • Quest rewards. On a quest's reward buttons, Alt+I opens the info card for a specific reward item so you can inspect what you would receive before accepting. See quests.
  • Caravan stat values. In caravan formation and info screens, Alt+I on a value breaks it down into the contributing factors. For example, caravan speed or carry capacity is the sum of several contributions, and the info card shows each one.

docs.title: Coverage
docs.text: Alt+I works in most places, but not absolutely everywhere yet. If you press it somewhere you expected an info card and nothing happens, that spot may not be wired up. If that happens on a screen where you think it belongs, let me know and I can take a look.

docs.title: Navigating menus
docs.text:
RimWorld has many screens, but they share a small set of navigation shapes. This page covers all of them. When you open something new, the first question is: which shape is it?

  • Tabs: separate panels, moved between with Tab and Shift+Tab.
  • Columns or categories: sections moved between with Left and Right arrows.
  • Tree views: lists that expand and collapse to reveal nested details.
  • Tables: a grid of rows (usually pawns) and columns (usually attributes or policies).

A few things work regardless of shape: you can start typing to jump to an item (type-ahead), and press Escape to back out. The rest of this page walks through each shape and the rules that connect them.

docs.title: Tabs (Tab / Shift+Tab)
docs.text:
Many screens are split into panels. Tab moves to the next panel; Shift+Tab moves to the previous one. This is not the classic "tab through every field" behavior from web forms. It moves between whole sections of a screen.

For example, the Work tab uses Tab and Shift+Tab to move between pawns, and the caravan formation screen uses them to move between the summary and formation panels. Once you land on a panel, arrow keys navigate within it.

A single tab can itself contain any of the other shapes: a panel might hold a tree view, a table, or a set of columns. Some screens are several tables side by side. Tab and Shift+Tab always move between the panels; once inside one, you navigate it by its own shape.

docs.title: Columns and categories (Left / Right arrows)
docs.text:
Some screens lay content out as sections you step through sideways. Left and Right move between those categories; Up and Down move within the current one.

The Quest menu is a clear example: Left and Right move between Available, Active, and Historical. Tables also use this pattern, where Left and Right move between columns.

docs.title: Tree views
docs.text:
A tree view is a list where items can contain other items. RimWorld uses these frequently because much of its information is dense and hierarchical. Expanding an item reveals everything inside it.

  • Right arrow expands the current item (reveals children).
  • Left arrow collapses it (hides children).
  • Up and Down move between items at the current level.
  • Shift+8 (asterisk / *) expands all expandable siblings at the current level, so you can arrow across them without expanding each one individually.
  • Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End jump to the absolute first or last item in the tree, regardless of nesting level.

When an item is collapsed, the mod speaks a short summary of what's inside, so you can decide whether to expand it. Some tree items hold controls (a checkbox, an adjustable value) as well as readable content, so expanding can reveal things you act on as well as things you read.

docs.title: Level announcements
docs.text: As you move up and down the tree, the mod announces the depth level when you change levels. This tells you where you are in the hierarchy without requiring you to track it mentally.

docs.title: The "Rashad Hates Treeviews" mode
docs.text:
There is an option that changes how trees behave, named after a fellow accessibility-mod developer. The label is "Rashad Hates Treeviews (Submenu-Style Navigation)" and it lives under Main Menu > Options > RimWorld Access. It is off by default.

With the setting off (standard mode): pressing Right on a collapsed item expands it and keeps the parent in view, with children listed below. Pressing Right on an already-expanded item drills into the first child.

With the setting on (submenu mode): pressing Right expands an item, hides the parent, and drops you onto the first child, like stepping into a submenu. Pressing Left collapses back to the parent. The mod remembers your position inside each parent, so stepping back in returns you to where you were.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text: A table is a grid. Rows are usually your pawns; columns are usually attributes or policies (medical care, apparel, a skill, a checkbox). Up and Down move between rows; Left and Right move between columns.

docs.title: Sorting (Alt+S)
docs.text: Press Alt+S to sort the table by the column you are on. Press it again to cycle: descending, ascending, no sort. This is how you find, say, your best constructor or your highest shooting skill.

docs.title: Painting a column
docs.text:
To copy one cell's value down (or up) an entire column without setting each cell individually:

  • Shift+Up / Shift+Down: paint the current cell's value onto the row above or below.
  • Shift+Home / Shift+End: paint from the current row to the top or to the bottom.
  • Ctrl+Shift+Home / Ctrl+Shift+End: paint the value across every row in the column, regardless of your current position.

docs.title: Editing cells
docs.text:
• Enter or Space toggles a checkbox cell.
  • = and - nudge a numeric cell up or down by one; Enter lets you type a number directly.
  • ] on a column header or cell opens a context menu of options for that category. See the context menu page for how that menu works.

docs.title: Type-ahead: start typing
docs.text: In any menu or list, start typing and the mod jumps to the first matching entry. This is one of the fastest ways to navigate. In a long Architect menu, type "wall" or "stock" to land directly on what you want instead of arrowing through dozens of entries. Type-ahead also works inside filter screens and search boxes when adding items by name. Press Enter to run whatever the search landed on. If you would rather arrive there and look around first, press Shift+Enter: the search ends and the item is read back without being activated.

docs.title: The Enter-vs-Alt+S rule
docs.text:
The question is always: on this screen, does Enter already do something to the current item?

  • If Enter selects or deselects items (checking a pawn into a caravan, toggling a choice), Enter is "busy." In that case, Alt+S confirms the screen and moves you to the next one. The starting-pawns and caravan-formation screens work this way.
  • If Enter does not do anything special to the current item, Enter finishes the screen. World-map site selection works this way: Enter settles on the tile.

Before assuming Enter will advance you, notice whether it is already doing selection work. If it is, use Alt+S to confirm. In tables, Alt+S is also the sort key, which fits the same logic: you are toggling and editing cells, so Enter is busy and Alt+S takes the confirm role.

docs.title: Escape
docs.text: Escape cancels or closes the current screen and steps you back one level. On the main map with nothing else open, Escape opens the pause menu.

docs.title: A quick checklist for any new screen
docs.text:
1. Press Tab once. If it moves you to a different panel, Tab and Shift+Tab navigate between them.
  2. Try Left and Right. If they move between sections while Up and Down move within a section, it is a columns or categories layout. If Up and Down step through rows (usually pawns) while Left and Right change which column you are reading, it is a table.
  3. Try Right on an item. If it expands, you are in a tree view (and Left collapses).
  4. Start typing. Type-ahead jumps to a match.
  5. To finish: check whether Enter is already doing selection work. If yes, confirm with Alt+S. If no, Enter finishes. Escape backs out.

docs.title: Selecting pawns
docs.text: Colonists (the game calls them pawns) are the heart of a RimWorld colony. This page covers how to select them, navigate the colonist bar, jump the cursor to a specific pawn, and build combat groups. For reading a pawn's health, mood, and other stats at a glance, see checking on pawns.

docs.title: The colonist bar
docs.text: The colonist bar is a persistent strip along the top of the screen that shows all your colonists and mechs. You can navigate it, select individual pawns, reorder it, and page through larger groups without touching the cursor.

docs.title: Cycling through colonists (comma / period)
docs.text: Period selects the next colonist; comma selects the previous one. This is the game's own vanilla cycling behavior: it steps through your colonists in bar order and announces the selected pawn. When you reach the mech section of the bar, the same keys cycle through mechs instead.

docs.title: Selecting by number (Alt+1–0)
docs.text:
Alt+1 through Alt+9 select the colonist at positions 1–9 on the current bar page. Alt+0 selects position 10.

Pressing the same Alt+number twice within about half a second also moves the cursor to that pawn's tile and snaps the camera to them. The single press selects and announces; the double press is the cursor jump.

docs.title: Paging through more than ten colonists (Alt+Down / Alt+Up)
docs.text: When you have more than ten colonists or mechs, they are organized into pages. Alt+Down pages to the next group; Alt+Up pages back. After paging, use Alt+1–0 to select within the new page.

docs.title: Navigating the bar one pawn at a time (Alt+Left / Alt+Right)
docs.text: Alt+Left and Alt+Right move through the colonist bar one pawn at a time, crossing page boundaries. This is a linear walk across the entire bar rather than a page-at-a-time jump.

docs.title: Reordering the bar (Ctrl+Alt+Left / Ctrl+Alt+Right)
docs.text:
Ctrl+Alt+Left and Ctrl+Alt+Right move the currently selected pawn earlier or later on the bar. This lets you arrange colonists in an order that makes sense to you, so the numbers fall where you expect.

Ctrl+Alt+Down and Ctrl+Alt+Up move the pawn between pages on the bar.

docs.title: Focusing the cursor pawn on the bar (/)
docs.text: Press / to focus the pawn under the cursor on the colonist bar. If the cursor is on a colonist or mech that appears on the bar, the bar jumps to that pawn's position. This is how you move quickly from "cursor on pawn" to "pawn selected on bar."

docs.title: Jumping the cursor to the selected pawn (Alt+C)
docs.text:
Press Alt+C to move the cursor and camera to the currently selected pawn. This is the reverse of /: it takes you from "pawn selected on bar" to "cursor on pawn." When several pawns are multi-selected, Alt+C opens a picker so you can choose which one to jump to.

After the jump, the cursor stays with that pawn. It rides along as they walk, silently, so pressing K tells you where they are right now rather than where they were when you jumped. Move the cursor any way you like, or select someone else, and it stops riding and is yours again. Press Alt+C again whenever you want to catch back up.

docs.title: Multi-select (Alt+Space)
docs.text:
Alt+Space toggles the pawn under the cursor (or the currently focused bar pawn) into or out of a multi-select group. Once multiple pawns are selected, orders issued via ] or gizmos apply to all of them.

Multi-select is mainly useful for combat: sending a group to attack a position, drafting several colonists at once, or setting up combat groups. Many gizmos expect a single pawn and will produce unexpected results (or not work at all) when multiple pawns are selected. If a gizmo behaves strangely, check whether multi-select is active.

Ctrl+Alt+Space selects all colonists at once, or clears the multi-select if already active.

Alt+Shift+Right and Alt+Shift+Left extend the current selection contiguously to the next or previous pawn on the bar.

docs.title: Combat groups (Ctrl+Shift+F1–F4 / Ctrl+F1–F4)
docs.text:
You can save and recall named groups of pawns for fast combat deployment.

  • Ctrl+Shift+F1 through Ctrl+Shift+F4 save the current multi-select group to slot 1–4.
  • Ctrl+F1 through Ctrl+F4 recall the saved group from slot 1–4, re-selecting those pawns.

Note: F1 by itself opens the Work menu; F2 opens the Schedule menu; F3 opens the Assign menu; F4 opens the Animals/Mechs menu. The combat group keys require Ctrl to avoid conflicting with those.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Checking on pawns: health, mood, needs, gear, and skills at a glance.
  • The context menu: issuing orders to a selected pawn at the cursor tile.
  • Gizmos: the command actions available for a selected pawn or object.

docs.title: The map
docs.text: The map is your colony: a grid of tiles where most of the game takes place. A cursor moves over it with the arrow keys, terrain under the cursor plays a distinct sound, and number keys provide on-demand information about a tile. This page covers getting around the map and controlling game time. For finding and jumping to specific things, see the scanner.

docs.title: Moving the cursor
docs.text:
The arrow keys move the cursor one tile at a time, with the camera following. Up, Down, Left, and Right work as you would expect.

As you move, the tile underfoot plays a terrain sound. Soil, stone, sand, water, and built flooring each have distinct audio cues, so with practice you can tell where you are by ear. Moving against a wall plays its own sound, which helps you trace room edges.

As you arrow around, the mod announces the name of what is under the cursor. Number keys are for deeper, on-demand detail rather than something you press after every step.

docs.title: What is on this tile? (number keys 1–7)
docs.text:
With the cursor on a tile, press a number key to hear a specific category of information about that tile. These are spot-checks; most of this information is also announced as you move.

  • 1 = items and pawns at the cursor
  • 2 = terrain (fertility, path cost, beauty, cleanliness)
  • 3 = harvestable things (plants and their growth, and with the right DLC or equipment, fish and deep-scanner mineral targets)
  • 4 = light (brightness) and temperature
  • 5 = room stats
  • 6 = power
  • 7 = areas

On the world map, the same number keys report different categories. That mapping is covered on the world map page.

docs.title: Jumping to coordinates (Ctrl+G)
docs.text: Press Ctrl+G to open the coordinate-jump dialog. Type an X coordinate, press Comma or Space to advance to the Z field, type a Z coordinate, and press Enter to jump. Leaving a field blank keeps the current coordinate. Entering +N or -N moves that many tiles relative to the current position. Escape cancels.

docs.title: Jump modes: covering ground fast
docs.text:
Tile-by-tile movement is fine for close work, but crossing the map one step at a time is slow. Jump modes let a single keypress leap to the next thing in a given direction. Four jump modes are available:

  • Preset distance: jumps a fixed number of tiles in the direction you choose.
  • Impassable: jumps to the last tile a colonist could walk to that way, stopping before a wall, a rock face, deep water, or anything else that would block a pawn.
  • Terrain: jumps to the next tile whose ground is different, so a stretch of sand or a paved floor crosses in one press.
  • Structure: jumps to the next tile whose building is different, so a run of marble wall crosses in one press and lands where that wall changes or ends. Standing on open ground, it finds the next building instead.

Blueprints and frames count as the thing they will become, so a colony under construction navigates like the one being built.

Controls:

  • Ctrl+arrow jumps in that direction using the active mode.
  • Shift+Up / Shift+Down cycle to the next or previous jump mode. The cursor does not move; the mod announces the new mode. In the three scanning modes, where there is no distance to adjust, Shift+Left and Shift+Right repeat the mode name.
  • Shift+Left / Shift+Right adjust the preset distance by 1.
  • Shift+Ctrl+Left / Shift+Ctrl+Right adjust the preset distance by 10.

The scanning modes cover an unpredictable number of tiles, so they announce the distance before describing where the cursor landed, for example "7 tiles. Marble wall." When there is nothing to jump to, the mod says so and stays put: "blocked", "no terrain change that way", "no structure change that way", or "map boundary".

No jump crosses into unexplored ground. A scan stops at the fog line, so a jump never tells you what is hiding in the dark.

Jump modes are also used when sizing a wall or zone during building placement. See the Architect menu page for that flow.

docs.title: Controlling time
docs.text:
RimWorld runs in real time when unpaused. You will pause often to think and give orders.

  • Space pauses and unpauses.
  • Shift+1 sets normal speed, Shift+2 sets fast, Shift+3 sets super-fast.
  • T announces the current in-game time, date, weather, and season. Press it twice: if the time has not changed, the game is paused.
  • Alt+T announces the current game speed and performance: speed name (Normal, Fast, etc.), actual and target ticks per second, and whether a threat is causing a forced slowdown.
  • ? (question mark) opens the Learning Helper, RimWorld's own built-in tips. Press Enter on a lesson to read it, Down to keep reading, choose "Mark as learned" and press Enter to dismiss a lesson. Escape closes the helper. These are the game's tutorial nudges, separate from this documentation.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• The scanner finds and jumps to anything on the map: a stretch of stony soil, a dropped weapon, the nearest geyser.
  • Checking on pawns covers selecting colonists and reading their health, mood, needs, gear, and skills.
  • The Architect menu is how you place buildings and zones.

docs.title: The scanner
docs.text:
The scanner finds and jumps to things on the current map or world map without hunting tile by tile. Looking for the nearest geyser, a dropped rifle, every patch of stony soil, or all the temperate forest tiles on the world? The scanner organizes what is out there into categories and lets you jump directly to any of it.

It works by drilling through levels: broad categories, then subcategories, then item types (ordered by distance), and finally individual instances of a type. Home jumps the cursor to whatever the scanner is currently pointing at.

docs.title: Key scheme
docs.text:
• Ctrl+Page Up / Ctrl+Page Down: move between categories (the broadest grouping).
  • Shift+Page Up / Shift+Page Down: move between subcategories within the current category.
  • Page Up / Page Down: move between item types within the current group, ordered by distance (nearest first).
  • Alt+Page Up / Alt+Page Down: step through the individual instances of the current type, one at a time (for example, "grass, 1 of 39").
  • Home: jump the cursor to the scanner's current target.
  • End: announce the distance and direction from the cursor to the current target.
  • Alt+Home: toggle scanner auto-jump mode (the cursor follows the scanner automatically as you step through items).

As you move through levels, the mod announces what you have landed on and how many there are. You might hear "12,977 grass tiles" at the type level, or "grass, 1 of 39" as you step through instances.

Not every category has subcategories. When one does not, work with categories, item types, and instances only.

docs.title: Clumps and the Home double-press
docs.text:
Many terrain types and items appear as contiguous patches rather than isolated tiles. The scanner groups these into a single clump entry and reports the tile count (for example, "fertile soil, 200 tiles").

Pressing Home once jumps the cursor to the tile in the clump nearest your current position. If you are now standing on the clump and it is large enough to have a distinct center, pressing Home a second time jumps to the clump's center. The mod offers the "press Home for center" hint only when a center jump is available.

docs.title: A typical flow
docs.text:
1. Use Ctrl+Page Up/Down to find the right category.
  2. If the category has subcategories, narrow down with Shift+Page Up/Down.
  3. Use Page Up/Down to pick the item type you want (nearest first).
  4. Press Home to jump the cursor to it. If there are many instances of the type, use Alt+Page Up/Down to step to the specific one you want, then Home.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
On the world map, finding biomes. Move to the biomes category with Ctrl+Page Up/Down, then use Page Up/Down to reach temperate forest. The mod reports how many there are, and Alt+Page Up/Down steps through each patch. Home jumps the cursor to the current one so you can check its tile info. Roads and settlements are available as their own categories.

On the colony map, finding terrain. Looking for stony soil to build a foundation? Drill into the terrain category, pick the terrain type (sorted by distance, so the closest patch appears first), and press Home to land on it. Press Home again from within the patch to jump to its center.

On the colony map, finding an item. You dropped a weapon somewhere in the chaos. The scanner groups items into categories and types; find weapons, narrow to the rifle, and Home jumps the cursor straight to it.

docs.title: Pairing the scanner with search
docs.text: Sometimes it is faster to name the thing you want. Press Z to open the map search, type what you are after, and press Enter to dismiss the search field. Matches become available as you type, so the scanner is then pointed at your results: step through them with the scanner keys and press Home to jump the cursor to one. Get in the habit of pressing Enter to close the field first, otherwise a later Enter just closes it when you meant to do something else.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• The map covers cursor movement, terrain audio, the number-key tile info, and jump modes.
  • The world map and choosing a site uses the scanner heavily when picking a landing spot.

docs.title: First launch
docs.text:
Launch RimWorld with the mod enabled and your screen reader running. The main menu should start talking right away. Use Up and Down to move through the menu items and Enter to select one.

If nothing speaks, make sure your screen reader is running and the Steam in-game overlay is turned off. Both are covered on the installation page.

docs.title: The RimWorld Access settings
docs.text:
The mod's settings live at Main Menu > Options > RimWorld Access. You can open that same screen from inside a game too: pause, open Options, find RimWorld Access.

The defaults are sensible, so there's nothing you have to change before playing. If you want to look around, the settings reference explains what each option does.

docs.title: Tutorial series
docs.text: I've recorded a tutorial series walking through the game from the beginning. Part 1 is up now, and more parts are coming. If you're new to RimWorld, it's worth watching as you find your feet.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text: To understand how the mod's controls work, read the Core Concepts section. It covers menus, the map, the scanner, and the handful of ideas that let you find your way around any screen in the game. To get better at RimWorld itself, see Where to learn RimWorld.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
This page walks through what you need to do before the mod will work, including turning off the Steam overlay and installing the mod files.

Having trouble?

If you get stuck on any step here, join the official RimWorld Access Discord server. Ask in the help channel and we will be happy to walk you through it.

docs.title: Turn off the Steam in-game overlay
docs.text:
Do this before anything else, for your sanity. This will benefit all your Steam games, not just RimWorld.

Steam's in-game overlay grabs certain key combinations like Shift+Tab before they reach RimWorld. The overlay itself is not screen-reader accessible, so when it is on, some of the mod's keys will silently do nothing and you will have no way to tell why.

Turn it off:

  1. Open Steam.
  2. Go to Steam menu > Settings.
  3. Select the In-Game tab.
  4. Uncheck "Enable the Steam Overlay while in-game."
  5. Close the Settings window.

If a key like Shift+Tab ever stops working, come back and check this first.

docs.title: Install the mod
docs.text: There are two ways to install RimWorld Access: through the Steam Workshop, or by hand. The Workshop is the easier path and keeps the mod up to date for you. Pick whichever fits, then finish with the shared step at the end that switches the mod on.

docs.title: Steam Workshop (recommended)
docs.text:
1. Log into Steam, open the RimWorld Access Workshop page, and click Subscribe.
  2. Steam will ask whether you also want to subscribe to Harmony, the other mod RimWorld Access depends on. Choose Subscribe to All.
  3. Both will automatically download the next time RimWorld launches.

That puts the files in place. Now read Turn the mod on.

docs.title: Manual install
docs.text:
Use this if you do not own RimWorld on Steam, or you would rather manage the files yourself.

Download the latest release and unzip it into RimWorld's Mods folder, so you end up with a RimWorldAccess folder inside Mods. With a default Steam install, the Mods folder can be found at the following locations:

  • Windows: C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\RimWorld\Mods
  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Steam/steamapps/common/RimWorld/RimWorldMac.app/Mods

If you installed RimWorld to a different Steam library, the path up to steamapps changes, but everything after it stays the same.

A manual install does not include Harmony. You will need to download it separately:

  • On Steam: Log into your Steam account in a web browser, open the Harmony Workshop page, and click Subscribe. Steam downloads it the next time the game launches.
  • Without Steam: Install Harmony from its GitHub releases page and place it in the same Mods folder.

docs.title: Turn the mod on
docs.text:
Regardless of how you installed it, the final step is the same. RimWorld's own mod list is not screen-reader accessible until RimWorld Access is already running, so instead of switching the mod on inside the game, you drop in a settings file that has it switched on already.

Download ModsConfig.xml and place it in RimWorld's Config folder. It comes ready-made with Harmony and RimWorld Access already enabled. The Config folder can be found at the following locations:

  • Windows: %localappdata%low\Ludeon Studios\RimWorld by Ludeon Studios\Config
  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/RimWorld/Config

You can paste either path as-is and it will open the correct folder. On Windows, paste it into the Run dialog (Win+R) or the File Explorer address bar. On macOS, paste it into Finder's Go to Folder box (Cmd+Shift+G).

docs.title: Already installed it by hand before?
docs.text:
If you installed an earlier version of RimWorld Access by hand, you may still have a RimWorldAccess folder in your Mods folder. After subscribing on the Workshop, it is worth deleting that folder, for two reasons:

  • A copy sitting in your Mods folder always loads instead of the Workshop copy. You could keep running an old version without realizing it, and it would not update automatically.
  • Older builds used a different mod identifier than the Workshop release. The two will not clash on their own, but if both end up enabled in your mods list, RimWorld might load the mod twice, which would probably break things.

The settings file above enables only a single copy, so as long as you use it and do not turn on a second one by hand, you are safe either way. Deleting the old folder just removes any chance of mixing them up.

docs.title: Launch the game
docs.text: Once the files are in place, launch RimWorld. With your screen reader running, the main menu should start talking immediately.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text: Head to first launch to learn more about getting started with the mod!

docs.title: Changelog Archive (Pre-2.0)
docs.text: The history of RimWorld Access before version 2.0, from the "Aaron's Unofficial Patch" era, preserved verbatim. Newest first.

docs.title: CHANGES
docs.text:
• Fixed digits typed into a quantity chooser also passing through to the screen behind it. Typeahead no longer leaks past quantity choosers.
  • Fixed the inventory showing item locations ("on", "carried by", etc.) in English for non-English players.

docs.title: CHANGES
docs.text:
• Fixed a freeze in the custom ideoligion builder where, after typing a name, adjective, or member name in Simplified Chinese and pressing Enter, the mod stopped responding to keys until you switched windows and back.
  • Fixed body parts in the health tab reading their condition and injuries twice.

docs.title: CHANGES
docs.text:
• Fixed the background music not starting after you create a new world and colony. You no longer have to restart the game for it to play.
  • Fixed entering custom numbers for bills at a workstation. Typing a quantity now goes into the number field instead of being swallowed by the menu's typeahead.
  • Fixed the research detail view mixing up which buildings were available. A bench you have built now reads as available even when a required facility like the multi-analyzer is missing, and each facility reports its own status: available, present but inactive, or not available.
  • Terrain sounds no longer play for tiles you have not discovered yet.
  • The world map tile information (press 4) no longer reads the internal Tile ID, which was developer data not meant for players.
  • Styling stations are now fully accessible. Tab moves between the hair, beard, face tattoo, body tattoo, and apparel color sections, and the arrow keys (with typeahead) browse the options. Enter applies a style and opens a color list so you can set its color in one step. Alt+S applies all your changes; Escape cancels.
  • Plans are now fully accessible. A new Plans scanner category groups your plans by color into subcategories, and after placing a plan you can configure it from the gizmo menu.
  • Every hairstyle, beard, and tattoo now has a written description of what it actually looks like, so you are no longer choosing by name alone.
  • Pawns now have an Appearance section in their inspect screen, listing hair and hair color, beard, tattoos, and favorite color in one place.
  • The paint designator's color picker is now accessible, and painted floors and buildings announce their color as you move the cursor over them.
  • Added a Roofs category to the scanner, covering both thin rock roofs and overhead mountains.
  • The Learning Helper now includes RimWorld Access lessons, and most of the game's own lessons have been edited with the mod in mind. Suggestions for more are welcome.
  • With a drafted pawn selected on the colonist bar, pressing 1 on a tile holding another pawn reads the game's shooting accuracy tooltip.
  • Removed the old unsupported cursor jump modes; only "preset distance" and "adjacent to walls" remain.
  • The mod info panel now shows the project website (rimworldaccess.com) as a link, and the description was rewritten to be shorter.
  • The mod is now available in Latin American Spanish and Russian. Like our other community translations, these are machine translations anchored to RimWorld's own official wording, so corrections from native speakers are welcome.

docs.title: CHANGES
docs.text:
• Added cursor sound for vacstone tiles.
  • On space and asteroid maps, the tile info key that reports light and temperature (4) now also reports the vacuum level for the current tile, shown only when there is vacuum present.
  • Fixed one more English leak reported by a Chinese player: the "X available" count on items in the form-caravan list now speaks in your language.
  • Fixed the G gizmo menu after a Home-key or scanner jump: it now shows the gizmos for the tile you landed on, not a colonist you had selected earlier.
  • Fixed the work priorities menu opening broken when a mech was selected; pressing F1 or Alt+W on a mech now opens on a real colonist instead.
  • Fixed map switching (Shift+Period / Shift+Comma) skipping loaded maps with no colonists, mechs, or animals, such as a gravship map left holding only a grav anchor after everyone shuttled off.

docs.title: CHANGES
docs.text: • Players using a Chinese, Japanese, or Korean input method can now search lists again. Instant type-ahead can't compose pinyin, so you open a search box on purpose: press / in a list menu (trade, animals, research, and so on) or Z for the map scanner, type your query, then press Enter or Escape to close it. Everyone else keeps the instant type-ahead they already had, unchanged.

docs.title: CHANGES
docs.text:
• Fixed Alt+letter shortcuts (Alt+B/Alt+A in trade, Alt+M in work priorities) breaking for players using a Chinese/Japanese/Korean input method.
  • Translated two more spots that spoke English: the "active/not set" summary in the custom ideoligion precepts list, and the "material" cost word on the architect build menu.
  • Fixed "Refuel from cargo" on passenger shuttles: typing an amount and pressing Enter once now correctly applies it and confirms.

docs.title: CHANGES
docs.text:
• Fixed type-ahead search in the info card. Some idiot (me) forgot to register the info card with the new type-ahead system I built, so typing a letter in the info card either did nothing (when opened with Alt+I) or jumped around the inspection screen underneath it. It is now registered and works correctly.
  • Tracked down more places where the mod still spoke English instead of your language, thanks to reports from players running it in Chinese. Fixed: the expand/collapse state on memes in the custom ideoligion editor; the "Name" column header in the skills table and the assign menu; the generic "material" cost word shown for a wall or other stuff-built thing before you pick a material; the "Faction Name" text-box label when naming your faction; the "Rename" label on the zone and storage-group rename buttons; the sort direction ("ascending"/"descending") read out when you sort a table column; the on/off state on toggle buttons in command menus; and the "Preview/Stop ritual sound" option in the ideoligion editor. Keep the reports coming.
  • The world route planner now reads its path directions in your language too. When you trace a planned route tile by tile, the "head north to waypoint 2" style guidance (and the "Destination" call-out at the end) was still coming out in English. The compass direction and the whole phrasing around it are now translated.

docs.title: CHANGES
docs.text:
• The Character tab now reads a pawn's age and birthday: their biological age (with chronological age alongside it when the two differ), the date they were born, and the full chronological and biological breakdown. It also now reads the rest of what the vanilla character card shows but we were leaving out: backstory title, what the pawn is incapable of, royal titles, ideoligion role, xenotype, and any abilities listed on the card. The pawn's info card ('i') Character tab gained the same age and birthday details, so both places match the game.
  • You can now type Simplified Chinese, Japanese, and Korean into the mod's text boxes and search fields. This is new, so if you use one of those languages, please let me know whether typing and searching work for you.

docs.title: ANNOUNCEMENTS
docs.text:
• Localization support begins today, as an early beta. The mod has been massively refactored so that everything it speaks can be translated, and two trial languages are included to start: Simplified Chinese and Ukrainian. A lot of strings are going to be missing translations at first (the mod speaks English wherever one is missing), so please report the ones you catch. I will not be expanding to more languages until players have caught most of them, because every missing string found later has to be fixed across every supported language at once. Once the trial languages stabilize, localization across all 29 of the game's supported languages is coming. To set expectations: the base game is not localized perfectly in all 29 languages, the DLCs are not localized in all 29 either, and neither are most third-party mods. I cannot help with any of that; the game's own localization is a community project, and the README document in the game's installation folder lists where to go if you want to contribute.
  • I intend to release this update officially by Sunday, documentation included. Steam Workshop support may not make it by Sunday, but the release itself will be a complete, official update with everything here built in.

docs.title: CHANGES
docs.text:
• Improved the process of planting Gauranlen trees and other plantable seeds. While planting, a temporary scanner category now lists every tile you can plant on, with a second subcategory holding only the spots far enough from buildings to avoid the reduced connection strength warning. Arrow keys call out each tile's plantability as you sweep, and cancelling that warning dialog now returns you to placement mode instead of throwing away the whole planting order.
  • Anomaly entity suppression: you can now toggle auto-suppression on or off for a held entity. On its activity gizmo, Enter toggles auto-suppression and right bracket still adjusts the suppression threshold, matching the psyfocus gizmo's Enter-and-slider layout. Previously only the threshold was reachable.
  • Potentially fixed situations where a pawn could still be reported as downed after reloading a save in which they are no longer downed. I was never able to reproduce the problem myself, so I cannot promise the fix works; if you have run into it, please let me know whether it is gone.

docs.title: CHANGES
docs.text: • The slave tab is now properly wired. It was built, but not actually connected to the button!

docs.title: CHANGES
docs.text:
• The Archonexus relocation endgame is now fully keyboard-accessible: choosing your colonists and items, picking your new colony's world tile, and reforming your ideoligion all work with the mod.
  • During that endgame you can create, load, or fully edit your new colony's ideoligion, just like the builder you use when starting a world.
  • Arrow-key navigation now names the roof above you instead of a generic "roofed" or "underground", so a thin rock roof, a solid overhead mountain, and a player-built roof are easy to tell apart.
  • Fish population reports moved from the terrain key (2) to the resource key (3), alongside plants and minerals. Key 3 now lists only the resources relevant to your tile.
  • You can now banish a colonist, and execute a guilty one. Both live on the Social section of a pawn's inspection screen and on the Actions tab of their info card, each with the game's own warning about what will happen.
  • The scanner now points you at the nearest tile of a patch (a biome, a vein of ore, a stretch of soil, a road or river) instead of its center, so you hear how far its closest edge is and whether you are already standing on it. Press Home to jump to that nearest tile; once you are on the patch, press Home again to jump to its center. The colony map and the world map work the same way.
  • You can now load colonists and items into a map portal the same way you load a caravan or transport pod. This covers entering an ancient complex, going down an Anomaly pit gate or insect lair, and hauling your loot back out through the exit. The enter and exit commands now open a Pawns and Items screen with full keyboard navigation. Before, that screen opened silently and you could only move pawns in one at a time through the right-bracket menu, with no way to bring items along.

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• In auto-jump mode, the scanner no longer reports every place it takes you as being right on top of you. It used to measure the distance after it had already moved you onto the target, so each jump sounded like it was zero tiles away. It now simply announces what is on each tile as you flip through the scanner.
  • Cleaned up the building inspection menu: the "Power Control", "Breakdown Status", and "Power" items are gone. They either duplicated the Overview or let you do things you shouldn't (flip power instantly). Use the toggle power command (G) and a colonist will flick the switch as normal.
  • Number keys, arrow keys, and letter shortcuts no longer "leak" through to whatever is underneath an open menu. With a menu open, pressing a number could announce tile info, and letter shortcuts (like Alt+A or the ] orders key) could fire or type into a search box. This is now theoretically fixed across every menu.
  • Typeahead search now works the same in every menu. While you are searching, Up/Down step through the matches and Home/End jump to the first and last, all without clearing your search, and each tells you where you are (for example "match 2 of 3").
  • Typing no longer jumps to the wrong list when one menu sits on top of another. Float menus opened over a menu (like the bills "add recipe" picker), menus opened over a pawn's inspection screen (Operations, surgery pickers, Health Settings), and the quantity boxes in caravan and pod-loading dialogs now all search the menu you are actually looking at.
  • The pawn and building inspection screens now support typeahead. Start typing to jump through the tree, including weapons, apparel, and inventory items by name. Inspection search also matches what's inside a node, not just its name.
  • In the drug policy editor, Escape now clears an active search before closing, and the drug list reports how many matches your search found. The growing-zone plant picker also steps through search results correctly.
  • The saved-ideoligion load list no longer locks up when it's empty; Escape closes it normally.
  • When editing an ideoligion's base precepts (cannibalism, corpses, drug use, and the like), you can now press Delete to remove a precept you set, following the game's own rules about which can be dropped.
  • Fixed Alt-key shortcuts like Alt+R not working on some non-US keyboard layouts, including AZERTY.

This is a milestone beta release for me. As of this update, every RimWorld DLC is essentially fully accessible with the mod. Anything still rough is either a convenience (mostly around gravship building) or a bug, and bugs get fixed as they come in. The headline this time is the custom ideoligion builder, but it was only possible because of a big overhaul to how text boxes work, so let's start there.

docs.title: CHANGES
docs.text:
• Text boxes are now real text boxes, or as close as we can get. There is an actual cursor you can move through your text with the arrow keys, or jump word by word by holding Ctrl. Hold Shift while moving to select text, and Backspace removes the character before the cursor (or whatever you have selected). The mod now also knows the difference between a single-line box, like a name, and a multi-line box, like a description, so in a multi-line box you can press Shift+Enter to start a new line. When you finish editing with Enter, the mod reads back what the field now says. Typeahead should also work on non-English keyboard layouts now, though I have not been able to test that myself.
  • The big one: you can now build your own custom ideoligions, just like sighted players do on the ideoligion setup screen. This has been a long time coming. The builder has two tabs, and you switch between them with Tab. The first tab lists every ideoligion in the game; the second tab shows whichever one is selected. Select your own ideoligion and the second tab becomes a full editor; select someone else's and it is a read-only viewer. The editor is one big expandable list. The game crams an enormous amount of information onto this screen, so when you expand an item you can arrow through it line by line and hear all of it at your own pace. Most items can be changed by pressing Enter on them, including your ideoligion's name and descriptions, so when in doubt, press Enter and see what happens. To move on to the next setup screen, press Alt+S. The right bracket key ( ] ) opens a menu of extra options, including saving an ideoligion you have built so you can load it again in future games.
  • Fair warning: building an ideoligion is genuinely complicated, even for sighted players. There are a LOT of moving parts. If you are new to the game, you may want to get comfortable first. But I'm not your mom. Do whatever you want!
  • Fluid ideoligions work the same way in-game. Once yours has earned enough development points to reform, open the ideoligion viewer and press Enter on the item that shows your development points to begin.
  • The focused Work view now reads the selected colonist's name when it opens.
  • The colonist skills table (Alt+P) now tells you how much experience each skill has toward its next level, not just the level. On a paused game you can rest on a skill and hear the numbers change as colonists learn.
  • The starting characters screen now gives each colonist a Relations category, listing who they're tied to in your starting group and how
  • "Daughter," "Lover," and the like - with each pawn's opinion in the tooltip. Press Enter on a relation to jump straight to that pawn.
  • That same screen now has a Team Skills tab. Press Tab to switch to it for a quick rundown of which starting pawn is best at each skill.
  • The world map scanner now finds rivers, not just roads.
  • Walls (built walls, natural rock, and closed doors) now play their own navigation sound instead of the sound of the ground beneath them. Terrain sounds were also evened out so the volumes are more consistent.

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text: • Returning to the main menu from inside a game while on the world map no longer leaves the menu unresponsive. The Enter key works again right away, so you can pick a menu option without getting stuck.

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text: • Screen reader speech works again on setups where JAWS (or another reader) had gone silent. A recent version of the underlying Prism speech library began treating NVDA as available even when it wasn't running, so on machines without NVDA active it selected NVDA and spoke nothing. The mod is now pinned to the last known-good Prism version until the upstream fix ships.

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• A pawn's Relations now show family ties correctly from both sides: a parent now lists their child as "Daughter" or "Son" instead of "Friend," and the opinion breakdown lines up. Thanks to BlindGuyNW for the PR.
  • Forming a caravan from a hitching spot now works correctly. I had no idea hitching spots had a form caravan gizmo till recently!
  • The Left and Right arrow keys no longer move the map cursor while the F12 menu (Factions and Ideology) is open.
  • The biosculpter pod's "Nutrition storage" option now opens the

correct filter when activated. Previously, pressing Enter on it did nothing.

  • When a targeting action is rejected for the same reason more than once in a row (for example, casting an ability on a pawn with no healable injuries), the screen reader now repeats the specific reason instead of falling back to a generic "Invalid target." The game suppresses duplicate on-screen messages, which previously hid the reason from screen reader users on the second and later tries.

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• Scanner now works when launching a shuttle from a caravan on the world map.
  • Picking a landing cell after a shuttle launch no longer announces "Select pawn to target".

docs.title: CHANGES
docs.text:
• Sanguophage accessibility pass:
  • Deathrest Capacity gizmo now reads its progress, bound building count, description, and the names of bound deathrest buildings.
  • Hemogen bar now reads its full tooltip (drain rates, consumption threshold, description).
  • On the Hemogen bar, Enter toggles "Allow hemogen packs"; right bracket sets the target value.
  • Bloodfeed and other ability targeting now announce cursor- side warnings like "Will kill" or "Will cause serious blood loss" before you confirm the action.

docs.title: CHANGES
docs.text: • Ctrl+A in shape placement now steps through scopes. The first press still selects the current enclosure (room or blueprint flood); a second press expands to the entire map. Ctrl+Shift+A steps back to the previous scope. Any manual point change clears the step history.

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• The resurrector mech serum (and other dual-target psicasts like Skip) now works correctly when picking a destination tile.
  • During targeting, picking a different pawn from the colonist bar (comma/period, Alt+1..n, Alt+Left/Right) used to interrupt the cast. Those hotkeys now move the cursor to that pawn instead, so you can press Enter to target them.

docs.title: NOTE
docs.text: The targeting system received deeper rework today. If you hit any new oddities mid-cast, please report them.

docs.title: CHANGES
docs.text: • Bills now read the produced item's full description (e.g. "Make duster... Makes 1 Duster, Work amount: 167, Crafting. {full description}") in both the recipe picker and the active bill row.

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• Health conditions in character creation no longer announce a stray "newline-period" between mechanical effects and the description.
  • Escape with an active typeahead in character creation now clears the search instead of opening the "discard starting colonists" dialog.
  • The pause menu cursor resets between game sessions, so reloading after "Quit to main menu" no longer lands the cursor on "Quit to main menu".
  • The schedule menu (F2) no longer says a trailing "." when the Announce Position setting is off.
  • The 5-key room info no longer reads role-relevant stats as "star, star, star..."; instead, those stats are suffixed with "Important for this type of room."
  • The storage settings screen now uses the modern treeview (matching sounds, Rashad Hates Treeviews submenu mode, search auto-expansion). Priority lives as a node at the top.
  • The bills' ingredient filter and the apparel/food/reading-policy filters also use the modern treeview, with the standard expand sound (replacing the old click sound).
  • Typeahead in filter screens now announces the full label and description (not just the bare label) plus the match position.
  • Pressing Enter or Space on a filter row clears the typeahead buffer, so the next Down arrow walks the full list.
  • "Allow rotten" / "Allow fresh" are now hidden in the bills' ingredient filter when no allowed ingredient could ever match — matching vanilla (e.g. minigun, bionic eye recipes).
  • Space and Enter now behave identically across all filter screens.

docs.title: CHANGES
docs.text: • Starting-pawn selection now folds each pawn's quick stats into the collapsed treeview label instead of announcing them only on Alt+R. Arrowing onto a collapsed pawn reads name, title, age, gender, traits, and top five skills with passions; expanding the pawn collapses the label back to just the name and title so the screen reader does not re-read the long form on every category visit. Alt+R no longer appends an extra summary — the rebuilt tree re-announces the new pawn automatically.

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text: • Pressing Home on a captured Anomaly entity in the scanner (e.g. a sightstealer on a holding platform) now jumps the cursor to the platform instead of saying "Item no longer exists". Distance and direction announcements for held entities are also now reported relative to the platform.

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• Gizmos for minified items at the cursor (e.g. an unloaded bedroll on a quest map) now announce "Install" the first time you open the gizmo menu, instead of incorrectly saying "Reinstall at...". The same fix applies to the Shift+letter hotkey collector, typeahead search, and the multi-match disambiguation menu, so any vanilla command whose label depends on the live selection (Designator_Install and similar) now resolves correctly in every announcement path.
  • Alt+Space when only one pawn is selected now starts multi-select with that pawn as the first item, instead of silently re-selecting them and announcing "deselected, selection cleared". Multi-select is now a sticky mode you enter and leave deliberately: pressing Alt+Space on the last remaining pawn in the multi-select list exits the mode, as does pressing control alt space. More specifically, control alt space will toggle between selecting all and selecting none.
The headline change: you can finally name your saves. The pause menu and the save/load screens also got a thorough polish pass.

docs.title: NEW FEATURES
docs.text:
• You can now type a custom save name. The save menu drops you in a text field pre-filled with your faction name -- type to replace it, or press Down arrow to pick an existing save to overwrite.
  • Save and load menus now announce each save's game version and flag autosaves, matching what sighted players see. Loading a save from a different version (or with a different mod list) now goes through RimWorld's compatibility warning dialog, and pressing Escape on that dialog returns you to the save list instead of dropping you out to the main menu.
  • Anomaly research projects announce their tier (basic or advanced) while you browse the research menu, so you know which kind of entity you'll need to study to advance them.

docs.title: PAUSE MENU POLISH
docs.text:
• Cursor position is preserved when you Escape out of a sub-menu (Save, Load, Options, Play Settings, Review Scenario), so you land back on the item you just used. Closing the pause menu with Escape resets the cursor for next time.
  • Quit to Main Menu and Quit to Desktop now use proper confirmation dialogs (matching the rest of the mod), and cancelling either one returns you to the pause menu where you left off.
  • Play Settings now returns you to the pause menu on Escape instead of kicking you out entirely.
  • Home and End jump to the first and last items in the pause menu.

docs.title: More BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• Starting an Anomaly research project no longer falsely claims your regular research project was paused -- Anomaly and regular research run on separate tracks, and the mod now only mentions a previous project when one was genuinely replaced.
  • Several save/load labels that were hardcoded English (Overwrite, Load, Save, "please enter a name", delete confirmation) now use RimWorld's translation keys, so non-English players hear them in their own language.

RimWorld Access - Changelog for Aaron's Unofficial Patch

The big one: broad Anomaly DLC support. Psychic rituals, turret packs, the Entity Codex, and the monolith dialogs all now work with Rimworld Access. The scanner grew an Entities category and an Unexplored category for fog-of-war areas. Alongside that, reverse designators like Cancel Orders finally respect their keyboard shortcuts, the mech bar is ordered like the mechs menu, tile-info hotkeys repeat without lag, and both the local and world map scanners are faster. Huge thanks to OlegTheSnowman for the Entity Codex and the unexplored-areas scanner contributions.

docs.title: NEW FEATURES
docs.text:
• Anomaly DLC support: a big accessibility pass across the DLC. Most of the DLC's content should be accessible now, but please reach out if something doesn't work. Psychic rituals (and Ideology rituals) now announce their expected duration and outcome description when the dialog opens, with cleaner per-pawn readouts. Turret packs and any other ranged targeting source (including modded ones) are caught by a generic targeting handler that announces label, target type, range, and offers R for distance/line-of-sight. Invisible entities are now actually invisible to the scanner and cursor, matching what sighted players see. The held-entity tab gained a full keyboard menu covering every vanilla row -- Containment Strength, Escape MTB, Study Interval, Knowledge Gain, Allow Medicine, Containment Mode, Extract Bioferrite -- with the vanilla mouseover tooltips read out as well.
  • Entity Codex (Anomaly DLC): keyboard-navigable with Up/Down, Home/End, and typeahead on entry name. Discovered entries announce category, description, and linked things; undiscovered entries use the vanilla "undiscovered" wording. Alt+I on a selected entry opens a picker over linked things (info card) and discovered research projects (jumps straight to the project in the research menu). Thanks to OlegTheSnowman for the PR.
  • Anomaly Settings dialog at character creation: When the DLC is enabled, you can access its settings by tabbing past the save mode setting during story teller / difficulty selection.
  • Scanner "Entities" category (Anomaly DLC): Has subcategories for captured entities, as well as hostile ones.
  • Scanner "Unexplored" category: fog-of-war regions are groupable scanner targets now ("unexplored area: 42 tiles, 15.2 tiles northeast, area 2 of 7"). Regions refresh as your pawns explore, and they are excluded from the scanner search (so typing a room name doesn't get drowned in fog results). Thanks to OlegTheSnowman for the PR.
  • Targeting announces min range and explosion radius: when a verb has a minimum range or an AoE radius, those are spoken alongside the normal range readout, so you know up front whether you're inside your own blast radius or too close to fire.
  • The Diabolus's health sphere cannon is now correctly supported by the mod.

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• Reverse designator shortcuts work now: gizmos like "Cancel", "Uninstall", and other reverse designators for the selected thing were silently ignoring their keyboard shortcuts. They now fire on their hotkey like every other gizmo.
  • Ideology convert on prisoners: selecting "Convert" on a prisoner was supposed to switch the interaction mode to Convert and confirm the target ideology -- instead the choice was ignored. It now applies the mode and confirms the ideology as expected.
  • Mech bar ordering: the mech bar was listing mechs in a different order than the mechs menu, and two-digit counts sorted wrong (mech 10 before mech 2). Now the bar matches the mechs menu order, and numeric labels sort numerically... or at least in the same order the mech menu sorts them.
  • Tile-info hotkey repeat: hitting 1 (or any tile-info number) twice in quick succession used to drop the second press for ~300 ms. That rate limit is gone; the key repeats the readout immediately every time you press it.
  • Inspection screen and quest labels localized: the top-level category headers and quest labels on the inspection tab were hardcoded English. They now use RimWorld's translation keys, so non-English players hear their own language again.
  • Fog of war no longer leaks info: pressing tile-info hotkeys on a fogged tile used to announce terrain, temperature, and contents that sighted players couldn't see. Fogged tiles are now suppressed to match vanilla -- no more peeking through the fog with a screen reader.
  • Scanner performance (local and world map): The scanner should be more responsive on busier maps. Auto jump mode should work once more.
  • Global shortcuts during rename dialogs and the Work table: typing a letter in a rename field or the Work table used to sometimes fire a global hotkey (e.g. hitting tab would open the architect menu). Global shortcuts are now blocked while those inputs have focus.
  • Alt/Ctrl character suppression: holding Alt or Ctrl and hitting a letter used to dispatch both the modifier combo and the bare character, so Alt+F could trigger F's unmodified action as well. The bare character is now suppressed when a modifier is held.
  • Multi-select survives save/load: loading a save while multiple pawns were selected sometimes left a stale ghost selection. The multi-select is now cleared on load.
  • Outfit stands groupable: The mod now supports grouping outfit stands, and it works identically to grouping shelves. Have fun grouping!

RimWorld Access - Changelog for Aaron's Unofficial Patch

A short round of fixes: C now forms caravans properly on the world map, the Work tab stays tidy when a colonist is lost mid-session, geyser overviews don't claim negative health, and Alt+B on veteran pawns is much snappier.

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• World-map caravan formation (C): the shortcut was announcing "Reform caravan only works on temporary maps" and then doing nothing else. It now falls through to the real world-map behavior, so pressing C at a selected settlement forms a caravan like it always should have. On actual temporary maps, C still reforms the caravan.
  • Work tab ghost rows: when a colonist was captured, killed, or otherwise left the player's faction while the Work tab was open, their slot stuck around -- tabbing onto them landed silently or broke the announcement. Both the focused and table views now refresh the colonist list on the fly, so lost colonists drop out immediately and the cursor stays on whichever pawn should be next.
  • Geyser health line: inspecting a geyser (or any other indestructible object) was displaying "Health: -1 % (-1 / 100)", because those things don't track hit points. Indestructible objects no longer get a health line at all, matching vanilla.
  • Alt+B combat log, much snappier: on pawns with long combat histories the log used to take half a second to render. The mod was formatting every past entry just to throw away all but the 10 most recent. It now only formats the 10 it actually shows -- a roughly 50x reduction of wasted work for veteran colonists.

RimWorld Access - Changelog for Aaron's Unofficial Patch

Two new table views (Work and Skills), Ideology's Gauranlen tree change-caste dialog is now keyboard-navigable, a handful of cursor tricks, and a healthy stack of fixes. Oleg is back with dryad caste accessibility -- thank you, Oleg.

docs.title: NEW FEATURES
docs.text:
• Dryad caste dialog (Ideology DLC): the Gauranlen tree change-caste dialog is now keyboard-navigable. Up/Down through the castes, Home/End to jump, Enter to select, and typeahead search on caste name. Each caste announces its details. Full vanilla translations

throughout, including game-provided descriptions like "dryads produce X every Y." Big thanks to OlegTheSnowman for the PR.

  • Work table view (Ctrl+Tab (Option+Tab on Mac OS) to swap): a full 2D view of every colonist against every work type, alongside the existing focused view. This table view is exactly how sighted people would see this screen. Sort by Alt+S, paint priorities down a column with Shift+Up/Down or Shift+Home/End, and set a priority for everyone with Shift+0-4. Ctrl+Tab (Option+Tab on Mac) swaps between focused and table views anywhere in the Work tab. The default view is saved in Options > RimWorld Access, so whichever you prefer can be your home.
  • Pawn skills table (Alt+P): a read-only 2D table of your colonists against all their skills. Columns are skills in vanilla order, cells announce level, passion, and descriptor ("medical: 15, burning passion, excellent"). Alt+S sorts by the current column (passion breaks ties, disabled pawns sink to the bottom). Typeahead on pawn name. At long last, a way to answer "who's actually good at medicine" without pressing enter on every colonist.
  • Need tooltips in the Needs tree: each need under the pawn Needs category is now expandable and announces what sighted players see on hover. Descriptions (with tags stripped), where the need comes from (trait, gene, ideo, hediff), joy recreation tolerances and on-map joy sources, caravan joy gain, mood break thresholds, food level in raw units where that's meaningful (e.g. Thrumbos), learning activities -- all now in the tree.
  • Shift+ finds gizmos without selection: gizmo hotkeys used to only fire while the owning thing was selected, which meant cursor-navigating over a bed and hitting Shift+ silently did nothing. Now Shift+ checks both your selection and whatever is under the cursor. One match fires directly; multiple matches open a float menu with each option labelled by gizmo, owner, hotkey, and description. (Reform Caravan moved off Shift+C to plain C so Shift+C is free for any gizmo bound to C.)
  • Ctrl+A in shape placement: fills both corners of the current shape for you. Inside an enclosed room, it matches the room extents. Inside an area ringed by walls or blueprints, a flood-fill finds the interior. Otherwise it takes the whole map. Great for a single Chop Wood order across the entire map. (This doesn't work with line shapes for obvious reasons!)
  • K on the local map announces the current cursor coordinates.
  • Alt+1-0 double-tapped jumps to that colonist: first tap still selects them on the bar; a second tap within half a second moves the cursor, snaps the camera, plays terrain audio, and announces "Jumped to {pawn}. {tile info}". Works in multi-select mode too, so you can jump to a specific pawn without having to pick them in the menu.
  • Pawn location now rides along with job announcements: Alt+1-0 and comma/period now include the room, zone, or stockpile a colonist is standing in (e.g. "Bob, in kitchen, cooking meals").
  • Active-quest deadlines: the quests list shows "Expires in X" for accepted quests with a bad-outcome deadline (taking priority over "Accepted X ago"), and the detail view now pulls in every activity and expiry block vanilla shows on hover. Not-yet-accepted quests get the localized expiry string too.
