  • Threat slowdown announcements are now opt-in: Options > RimWorld Access > Announce Forced Slowdowns (default off). If you liked hearing "slowed by threat" every raid, turn it on; otherwise, peace.

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• Ideology preset chooser: Create Fluid, Create Fixed, and Load Saved are announced as "Accessibility coming soon" and blocked rather than silently dropping you into an inaccessible page. The one working option, Simple ideoligion, still works as before.
  • Prisoner tab: arrow keys, Enter, and Escape no longer leak into the inspection tree underneath. Hardcoded English labels swapped for vanilla translation keys, royalty recruitment offset surfaced, Anomaly study/knowledge info included, medical care section hidden for slaves (vanilla only shows it for prisoners), and executing a slave from a neutral faction asks for confirmation first.
  • Scanner search deduped: a single fence could show up three times in search results (once per subcategory it belonged to). Map search now reads from a single canonical list. World search also collapses landmarks whose labels differ slightly across the "All" and type subcategories down to one entry.
  • Typeahead ranking: the shortest-name tiebreaker used to treat a whole item label ("Butcher table: 75 wood. A heavy table for cutting...") as the "name," so typing "table" ranked anything whose description mentioned a table alongside items actually called table-something. Labels are now split at the first ": " / ". " boundary -- the name tiers only look at the actual name, and cost annotations and descriptions fall through to the Description tier. "Wall" still ranks before "Wall lamp."
  • Plants no longer claim a Growth Info tab. Vanilla doesn't have one. Growth %, conditions, blight, ready-to-harvest, and dying-reason details are already in the Overview category via the game's own inspect string. The invented tab was also displaying plant age as raw ticks ("1164000 / 90.4 days").
  • Full-map shape placement lag: rect/oval placement over large areas (a Chop Wood across the whole map, ~65k cells) used to freeze the game for a second or two. This was a mod bug, and has been fixed.
  • Work tab polish:
  • Pressing numbers while in basic view no longer secretly adjusts priorities in manual mode.
  • Quite a few tool tips were missing, the mod now reads them out.
  • Manual-mode disabled labels use "Priority 0" / "0" (vanilla's scale) instead of "off" / "Disabled".
  • 2D tables announce only the axis that actually changed: moving up/down in Animals, Wildlife, Mechs, Assign, Work table, Pawn Skills, Schedule, or AutoSlaughter no longer repeats the column name on every row change, and moving left/right no longer repeats the pawn name. Initial entry, post-sort, restore, and typeahead jumps still get the full context, since those are re-orientation moments.

RimWorld Access - Changelog for Aaron's Unofficial Patch
Bug fixes, typeahead and navigation improvements, character creation polish, and a couple of new keyboard shortcuts. The spatial audio footstep system introduced on 04/10 has been removed.

docs.title: A NOTE ON FOOTSTEPS
docs.text:
The positional footstep system from the 04/10 patch has been removed in this release.

After living with it for a few days, I couldn't get footsteps to the quality bar I wanted to put my name on. RimWorld's sound stage fights the integration: footstep positions don't track with a pawn's other sounds (so a cooking pawn who starts walking sounds out of place relative to its cooking sound), and reverb behavior was inconsistent in ways I couldn't tame. I had hoped the feature would be most useful in combat, but even after a lot of time tuning per-category volume sliders, footsteps either drowned out game audio, shattering immersion, or were too quiet to carry information. There was no middle ground I was happy to ship.

Huge thanks to OlegTheSnowman, who did the original contribution this system was built on. Oleg is of course free to continue this work in their own mod, as they were doing before. I may return to positional audio later, but for now I'd rather focus on the systems and DLC coverage already in the mod, documentation, and the long tail of bugs.

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• Prison beds: marking a bed for prisoners through the accessibility menu now updates the room's cached "prison cell" flag immediately. Previously the game didn't recognize the cell until you reloaded the save, which made "capture" and "arrest" jobs report "no available prison cells" even when you'd just set one up.
  • Mortar shells filter: the Shells tab wasn't opening when pressing Enter because of an internal name mismatch. Filtering which shells mortars will load works again.
  • Scanner category counts: each category's announced total was double- counting (sometimes more) because items appear in both their specialized subcategory and the "All" bucket. Counts now match what Page Up/Page Down can actually reach. Same fix applied on the world scanner.
  • Health capacity breakdown: expanding a capacity node (e.g. Moving, Manipulation) on the health tree now correctly announces what's affecting it -- the "Affected by" list of hediffs, injured body parts, and pain. An early-return bug had been silently dropping it.
  • Float-menu targeters accessible: second-stage targeting started from a float menu option (most visibly "Force target to wear/equip [apparel]") used to open silently with no screen reader feedback. Now announced and routable through the standard item targeting state. Generalizes to modded options that use the same pattern.
  • Submenus no longer close the inspection tree: opening a submenu (Bills, Range Edit, ThingFilter, Flickable, Refuelable, Breakdownable, Door Control, Forbid Control, Fishing Zone, Storage, Plant Selection, Bed Assignment, Owner Assignment, Prisoner tab, Info Card, etc.) used to dump you back to the map on Escape. You now return to the inspection row you launched from.
  • Refuelable buildings use the game's real fuel label: mortars show "Barrel durability", uranium slug turrets show "Uranium slugs", foam turrets show "Foam", deathrest caskets show "Hemogen", etc., instead of a generic "Fuel Settings".
  • Inapplicable ThingFilter options hidden: filters like "Allow rotten" and "Allow fresh" are hidden when no allowed item in the filter can ever rot. The mortar shells filter in particular now hides hit-point and quality options that don't apply to ammunition.

docs.title: CHARACTER CREATION
docs.text:
• Escape on the starting-pawns screen now asks for confirmation before discarding your rolled colonists.
  • Pawns and hediffs in char gen are no longer marked inspectable -- the tree already surfaces every stat inline, so the extra info-card step was redundant. Hediffs now announce their full description directly. Items and xenotypes are still inspectable.
  • ] context menu in char gen now routes reroll and rename through the same code path as Alt+R / Alt+N, so filter-aware announcements and

pawn filters now work correctly.

  • Reroll no longer loses your tree position when filters are active and the first attempt matches, and no longer loses position in "Rashad Hates Treeviews" submenu mode.
  • "Selected" and "Left behind" section headers now announce as info-card-style section boundaries only when you cross between sections, instead of taking up a navigable row each.

docs.title: WORK, SCHEDULE, ASSIGN
docs.text:
• Work menu now plays the same audio cues as vanilla. E.g. when you prioritize a job for which a pawn is ill suited.
  • Work, Schedule, and Assign all order pawns by their colonist-bar position now.
  • Assign also pulls in off-map colonists (caravans, travelling transporters) to match the vanilla Assign tab.

docs.title: TYPEAHEAD SEARCH
docs.text:
• Shorter names now rank first within each match tier across all menus that use typeahead. Typing "wall" lands on "Wall" before "Wall lamp".
  • Architect tree (Tab) and colony inventory (I) now auto-expand structural nodes on the first typed character so search reaches the whole tree without pressing '' first. The original tree shape is restored on Escape, Home/End, or deleting back to an empty query. Committing to a result (Enter, Left/Right, '') keeps the expansion.

docs.title: NEW KEYBOARD SHORTCUTS
docs.text:
• / (slash): focus the colonist/mech bar on whichever pawn is under the map cursor. Selects them, jumps the camera, and syncs the bar position so subsequent comma/period/Alt+arrow navigation picks up from the cursor. Announces "Not on colonist bar" if the cursor isn't on a bar pawn.
  • [ (left bracket): execute the TOP option of the context menu ] builds. Shift+[ queues the order (same as shift-click queueing in vanilla). Announces "PawnName: action" on single selection, and the familiar "Everyone X" / "Only A X" wrapping on multi-select.
  • Terrain announcements on cursor movement can now be toggled off under RimWorld Access (default on). When off, terrain names are suppressed from tile summaries during arrow-key movement, scanner Home jumps, bookmark jumps, and Go To. Terrain sound effects are unaffected.

docs.title: GIZMO HOTKEYS NOW REQUIRE SHIFT
docs.text:
Bare-letter gizmo hotkeys no longer fire -- you must hold Shift (e.g. Shift+K to build a wall). This frees up bare letters for other accessibility shortcuts and prevents accidental gizmo activation during navigation.

  • Draft (default R) is exempt. R still drafts/undrafts without Shift, since players rely on that muscle memory and no other gizmo shares R on a draftable pawn.
  • The hotkey is now announced immediately after the gizmo title, before the description and any cost/range/cooldown info, so you don't have to wait through a long description to hear the key.
  • Shift+T previously announced performance stats. Performance stats have moved to Alt+T so Shift+T can reach gizmos bound to T.

RimWorld Access - Changelog for Aaron's Unofficial Patch

Spatial audio footsteps, a major scanner rework, new inspection tabs, health overhaul, Mechs tab, gizmo slider/right-click support, mods menu redesign, and numerous fixes.

This patch has a lot of changes under the hood, so it may be a bit less stable than some of the others. I will release hot fix patches as needed throughout the weekend to ensure people can play comfortably!

docs.title: SPATIAL AUDIO (FOOTSTEPS)
docs.text:
A new positional audio system lets you hear pawns moving around your colony. Based on original work by OlegTheSnowman.

  • Terrain-aware footsteps: dirt, stone, wood, metal, carpet, bridge, water, snow — over 100 terrain types mapped via defName
  • Animal footsteps: light and heavy categories based on body size
  • Mechanoid footsteps
  • Stereo panning based on screen position relative to camera
  • Distance-based volume with near/mid/far field zones
  • Wall occlusion: sounds muffled through walls via low-pass filter, open doors partially restore clarity
  • Room reverb using RimWorld's room/region system
  • Interaural time delay for spatial precision
  • Zoom-level volume scaling
  • Per-category volume sliders (human, animal, mechanoid)
  • Performance mode with priority-based throttling (18/tick cap), prioritizing selected, drafted, and hostile pawns
  • Master "Enable Sound Effects" toggle
  • Cursor terrain sounds now share the same .ogg pool as pawn footsteps with room-aware reverb
  • All settings accessible via the keyboard-navigable options menu

docs.title: SCANNER REWORK
docs.text:
Major rework of the map scanner with better categorization, live updates, and smarter navigation:

  • New "All" top-level category listing every item closest-first
  • Each category also gets an "All" subcategory — Ctrl+PgDn lands on the All view, Shift+PgDn drills into specialized buckets
  • Pawns now split by faction: Colonists, Prisoners, Slaves, Guests, Hostile, Player Mechs, Hostile Mechs — raids during friendly visits no longer mix raiders and visitors
  • Many more natural terrain types show up (mud, moss, riverbank, lava, volcanic rock, etc.) — terrain detection uses fertility and pathCost instead of hardcoded English defNames, so DLC and modded terrain are caught automatically
  • Dead pawns and destroyed items detected mid-navigation with an "Item no longer exists" notice
  • Standing on a zone, stockpile, or terrain patch now reads "here" instead of pointing to the geometric center
  • Multi-region terrain shows specific area info ("10x10, here, area 1 of 63") instead of misleading totals
  • Page Up/Down preserves your position when the list re-sorts
  • Stable sort tie-breaking: items at equal distance no longer bounce between each other on every press
  • Harvestable subcategories now require plants to be fully mature
  • Minified items (uninstalled beds, tables, monument markers) now show their real names instead of "minified thing"
  • Ctrl+Shift+Left/Right adjusts preset jump distance by 10 tiles

docs.title: HEALTH INSPECTION OVERHAUL
docs.text:
The health section of the inspection tree has been modernized to match vanilla's structure:

  • Conditions grouped by body part instead of a flat "Conditions" list
  • Pain and bleeding (including time-to-death) shown upfront
  • Capacities use vanilla's pawn-type-specific labels and filtering
  • Collapsed summaries show full content without needing to expand

Operations menu improvements:

  • Typeahead search across all menu levels
  • Ctrl+Up/Down to reorder operations
  • Richer operation details: skill requirements, ingredients, replaced parts
  • Self-tend validation matching vanilla behavior

Alt+H quick health:

  • Now a focused combat triage readout: only sight, manipulation, and moving capacities are shown when not at 100% (the three that matter most for combat decisions)
  • Only damaged body parts (with HP) and bleeding with time-to-death
  • Bionics and chronic conditions filtered out

Localization improved throughout with vanilla translation keys.

docs.title: NEW INSPECTION TABS
docs.text:
Seven inspect tabs upgraded from generic text to full treeview content:

  • Feeding tab (Biotech babies): auto-breastfeed section with per-feeder mode selection (Never/Childcare/Urgent) and baby food toggles
  • Art tab: title and generated description
  • Book tab: benefits, dangers, and flavor text
  • Bookcase contents: list of books with Delete key to eject
  • Wind turbine auto-cut: toggle and Cut Now action
  • Guest tab: medical care selection via float menu
  • Transporter contents: items-to-load and contained-items with Delete to drop

Training tab (tamed animals):

  • Master assignment and follow toggles
  • Odyssey DLC behavior toggles
  • Trainable skill management

docs.title: MECHS TAB (Biotech DLC)
docs.text:
The Mechs tab is now fully accessible — the last main game tab to get screen reader support.

Press F4 to open. If you have only animals, it opens Animals. If you have only mechs, it opens Mechs. If you have both, a chooser menu lets you pick.

8 columns matching vanilla: Name, Energy, Draft, Auto Repair, Overseer, Control Group, Work Mode, and Allowed Area.

Interactive columns:

  • Draft and Auto Repair: toggle with Enter
  • Control Group: submenu to reassign between overseer's groups
  • Work Mode: submenu to change control group work mode
  • Allowed Area: submenu with Manage Areas support

Sorting via Alt+S. Full painting support via Shift+Up/Down and Shift/Ctrl+Shift+Home/End for Draft, Auto Repair, Control Group, and Allowed Area columns.

docs.title: GIZMO IMPROVEMENTS
docs.text:
Right-click options:

  • Right bracket on gizmos with right-click options opens them in a float menu (covers "Designate All", Command_Hide subclasses, and mechanitor control group gizmos)

Slider adjustment:

  • Enter on slider gizmos (fuel, hemogen, pruning, mech carrier) enters adjustment mode
  • Left/Right arrows step one increment, Shift for 5x
  • Heat/Psyfocus gizmo uses right bracket instead (Enter toggles the neural heat limiter)
  • Plays vanilla's DragSlider sound on each step

Also includes discoverability hints and psyfocus target value in announcements.

docs.title: MODS MENU REDESIGN
docs.text:
The mods menu has been rebuilt as a navigable two-level interface:

List level:

  • Up/Down to navigate, Left/Right to switch columns
  • Space to quick toggle enable/disable
  • Enter to open detail view

Detail level:

  • Navigable content lines: author, ID, versions, warnings, errors, requirements, and description
  • Action buttons: Enable/Disable, Mod Options, Website, Workshop, Open Folder, Unsubscribe
  • Open Folder now works on macOS and Linux (not just Windows)
  • Fixed Space quick toggle showing stale "Now on/off" announcements

docs.title: TABLE SORTING FIX
docs.text:
Sorting in the Animals, Wildlife, and Assign tabs now uses the game's own PawnColumnWorker.Compare() method instead of custom string-based sorting. This fixes broken sorting for non-English players and ensures correct ordering (e.g., training progress by level, not alphabetically).

Also adds 3-state sort cycle matching vanilla: descending → ascending → clear (return to default order).

docs.title: OTHER IMPROVEMENTS
docs.text:
• Shift+T announces game performance: current time speed, actual vs target ticks per second, percent of requested speed. When a combat threat forces normal speed, the announcement says "slowed by threat"
  • Time control labels now use vanilla translation keys (ClockTime, ClockDate, Weather, AM, PM, etc.) for non-English players
  • History messages tab: content announced first (then type, then date) so you can stop listening sooner. Alt+L/Alt+M filter hints announced on tab entry
  • Schedule - Allowed areas column: Shift+Home/End bulk paints allowed area to all pawns above/below, Ctrl+Shift+Home/End paints to all pawns
  • Bookmarks: double-tapping Ctrl+number now announces "Jumped" so you know you were moved
  • Pawn group shortcuts changed: save groups now Ctrl+Shift+F1-F4, recall groups now Ctrl+F1-F4 (avoids Alt+F4 closing the game on Windows and Cmd+F5 toggling VoiceOver on macOS)
  • Double-tap Ctrl+number to jump to bookmark as alternative to Ctrl+Shift+number (avoids keyboard layout switching conflicts)

docs.title: SCREEN READER FIXES
docs.text:
• Optional Tolk fallback for Windows: players can place Tolk.dll at %APPDATA%..\LocalLow\Ludeon Studios\RimWorld by Ludeon Studios to use Tolk instead of Prism for screen readers not yet supported by Prism
  • Fixed Prism config struct size for v0.11+ API (was causing initialization failure on all platforms)
  • Angle brackets in speech text no longer trigger SSML parsing on macOS, fixing silent or broken speech output
  • On macOS without VoiceOver, key presses now interrupt queued AVSpeechSynthesizer speech

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• Fixed terrain sounds not playing in non-English languages (was matching against translated labels instead of defNames)
  • Fixed non-Latin keyboard typeahead: Cyrillic and other non-Latin keyboard users can now search in menus (typeahead uses layout-aware character events instead of physical key codes)
  • Fixed maps with only mechs or animals being excluded from Shift+comma/period map switching. Map switch announcement now describes what's on each map (e.g. "3 colonists, 2 mechs")
  • Fixed input stealing during overlay/placement: float menus opened over placement mode now receive keyboard input correctly
  • Fixed designator loss when selecting a pawn during shape placement
  • Fixed "Unrestricted" area label not being localized in Animals tab

There's probably a lot more, honestly. It's hard to remember everything.
Cross-platform support (macOS and in theory Linux), Rashad Hates Treeviews fixes, and info card announcement improvements.

docs.title: CROSS-PLATFORM SUPPORT
docs.text:
RimWorld Access now works on macOS in addition to Windows. Linux is also supported in theory but has not been tested. The same mod package works across all three platforms — no separate downloads needed.

The mod has been migrated from the Windows-only Tolk library to Prism, a modern cross-platform screen reader abstraction layer. Prism auto-detects and uses the best available screen reader or TTS engine on your system:

  • Windows: NVDA, JAWS, SAPI, ZDSR, possibly others.
  • macOS: VoiceOver
  • Linux: Orca (untested)

macOS keyboard shortcuts: All keyboard shortcuts work identically to Windows with two substitutions:

  • Ctrl → Cmd (Command key)
  • Alt → Option key

Everything else is the same.

macOS installation: Place the RimWorldAccess mod folder at: ~/Library/Application Support/steam/steamapps/common/RimWorld/RimWorldMac.app/Mods

Known issues on macOS:

  • VoiceOver interruptions: incoming alerts and notifications will cut off whatever VoiceOver is currently reading. If you're in the middle of listening to something and an alert arrives, VoiceOver switches to the alert and you'll need to re-read the original content.

docs.title: Rashad Hates Treeviews fixes
docs.text:
Several fixes to the submenu-style navigation mode:

  • When opening inspection via Ctrl+Alt+Enter, the cursor now correctly lands on the first child item instead of the second
  • Section boundary announcements are now spoken before the item instead of after (e.g., "Gear. Steel sword" instead of "Steel sword. Gear"), giving you context first
  • Section names now use the short form instead of the full collapsed label, which could be very long for some categories
  • Expanding a node or opening inspection no longer redundantly announces the section or parent name — you just chose to go there, so you already know where you are. Section announcements now only fire when navigating up/down across section boundaries.
  • These fixes apply to both the inspect panel and the info card

Treeview overhaul with unified navigation and audio feedback, a new submenu-style navigation mode, smart labels, multi-select, launch destination filtering, world map landmarks, and info card improvements.

docs.title: MULTI-SELECT
docs.text:
A complete multi-select system that lets you select multiple pawns and issue group commands, eliminating the need to individually select and command each pawn one at a time.

Selection:

  • Alt+Shift+Left/Right: extend selection to adjacent pawns
  • Alt+Space: toggle individual pawns in/out of selection
  • Alt+Ctrl+Space: select all colonists / clear all selection

Persistent groups (3 slots):

  • Ctrl+Alt+F1 through Ctrl+Alt+F3: save current selection to a group
  • Alt+F1 through Alt+F3: recall a saved group

Groups persist across save/load. Pawns on other maps are filtered out on recall and announced as unavailable.

Navigation in multi-select mode:

  • Comma/Period, Alt+Left/Right, Alt+1-0, Alt+Up/Down all move focus without changing the selection
  • Camera does not follow focus movement
  • Focused pawn announces selected/not-selected status and current job

Group commands:

  • R: draft/undraft (toggles pawns matching the first pawn's state)
  • G: show gizmos for selected pawns (grouped like vanilla)
  • Right bracket (]): context menu for selected group
  • "Go here (formation)": line formation movement with two-point placement (Space to set points, Enter to confirm, Escape to cancel)

After issuing commands, you get smart feedback:

  • "Everyone drafted" / "Everyone except Bob, Sarah drafted" / "Only Carol, Dave drafted"

Pawn info shortcuts (Alt+H/M/N/K/G/B) use the cursor pawn first, then show a pawn picker menu if multiple are selected. Alt+C opens a pawn picker for camera jump. All pickers support typeahead search.

docs.title: TREEVIEW OVERHAUL
docs.text:
All treeviews across the mod now share a single unified navigation system. This means every tree in the game — architect menu, inspect panel, info card, ideology viewer, character creation, research menu, and more — behaves consistently with the same keyboard shortcuts and the same navigation rules.

Expanding and collapsing nodes now plays distinct sounds so you always know what just happened without needing speech. Especially useful for the new Rashad Hates Treeviews mode. Bulk-expanding with * plays a reverb version of the expand sound to signal that multiple nodes opened at once.

docs.title: Rashad Hates Treeviews Mode  (Optional Setting)
docs.text:
A new setting (off by default) transforms every treeview in the mod into submenu-style navigation for players who prefer an arguably better, but potentially more confusing, experience. When enabled:

  • Right Arrow or Enter on a category opens it like a submenu — the category disappears and you land on its first child
  • Left Arrow goes back to the parent, which reappears with the cursor on it
  • The tree remembers where you were in each category, so re-entering puts you right back where you left off
  • Crossing between expanded categories announces the new parent's name as a boundary cue
  • All other navigation (Home, End, typeahead search, etc.) works as usual

This is dedicated to Rashad, whose passionate hatred of treeviews inspired me to bring this back! Enable it in the mod settings under "Rashad Hates Treeviews."

docs.title: SMART LABELS
docs.text:
Data heavy Treeview nodes now show context-aware labels. When a node is collapsed, it shows a full summary of its contents. When expanded, it shows just the title — since you can already see the children. Expanding or collapsing always announces the short form so you're not overwhelmed with repeated information.

A new "Announce Levels" setting lets you toggle depth level announcements in treeviews (e.g., "level 2"). Turn it off if you find the level callouts distracting; turn it on if you want to stay oriented in deeply nested trees.

docs.title: LAUNCH DESTINATION FILTERING
docs.text:
When launching gravships, transport pods, or shuttles, the world map scanner now only shows destinations that are actually in range of the launch point. Previously the scanner listed every settlement, site, and tile on the map regardless of whether you could reach it — now unreachable destinations are filtered out automatically.

As before, fuel cost to each destination is announced as part of the tile summary, so you can factor costs into your decision-making.

docs.title: LANDMARKS (Odyssey DLC)
docs.text:
A new "Landmarks" category has been added to the world map scanner. This feature requires the Odyssey DLC — if you don't have Odyssey enabled, you won't see the Landmarks category in the scanner.

Landmarks are notable world features like mountain ranges, lakes, and volcanic fields. Each landmark's name is also included in the tile summary when you're standing on a tile that belongs to one. You can press 5 to learn more about the landmark.

docs.title: INFO CARD IMPROVEMENTS
docs.text:
The info card now uses section-based navigation instead of showing category headers as separate items you have to arrow past. Sections like Basics, Combat, and Apparel are announced when you cross from one section into another (e.g., "Combat section. Armor — Sharp: 50%"). This reduces clutter and makes browsing stats faster.

Stat entries that duplicate their category name no longer show redundant text.

docs.title: BUG FIXES AND SMALLER CHANGES
docs.text:
• Pressing Escape in the character creation pawn filter now saves your filters instead of discarding them
  • World map layer cycling changed from L to Tab/Shift+Tab for better consistency with other navigation patterns
  • Orbit (space) tiles no longer announce meaningless temperature and hilliness values
  • Pressing Enter on a gravship ritual role now changes the role assignment instead of accidentally launching the gravship
  • New pawns during character creation now announce their age, traits, and top 3 skills when rolled
  • Fixed duplicate skill announcements in ritual pawn selection
  • Fixed stale architect menu state persisting after switching to the world map
Map bookmarks, a fully accessible Learning Helper, and keyboard input fixes for AZERTY layouts, auto slaughter typeahead, and health tab operations.

docs.title: MAP BOOKMARKS
docs.text:
You can now save and jump to up to 10 bookmarked positions on each map. Bookmarks are saved per-map and persist across save/load.

  • Ctrl+Alt+1 through Ctrl+Alt+0: Set a bookmark at your current cursor position. You'll hear a confirmation with the tile summary (e.g., "Bookmark 3 set: Steel wall, Home zone").
  • Ctrl+1 through Ctrl+0: Announce a bookmark's info without moving. Reports the tile contents, distance, and direction from your current position (e.g., "grav engine, Gravship substructure, 189, 231, 13 tiles Southwest"). If the bookmark isn't set, you'll hear "Bookmark 3 not set".
  • Ctrl+Shift+1 through Ctrl+Shift+0: Jump your cursor directly to the bookmarked tile.

Bookmarks are stored independently per map, so your colony map bookmarks won't interfere with bookmarks on other maps. They persist when you save and reload your game.

docs.title: LEARNING HELPER
docs.text:
RimWorld's Learning Helper — the contextual tutorial that teaches game mechanics as you play — is now fully accessible via keyboard. When adaptive training is enabled (the default), new lessons are announced automatically through your screen reader as they activate during gameplay.

Press ? (question mark) to open the Learning Helper menu at any time while in-game.

The menu has two modes, toggled with Tab:

  • Active Lessons (default): Shows only currently active or unlearned concepts — the ones the game thinks are relevant to what you're doing right now.
  • All Lessons: Shows every tutorial concept in the game, with typeahead search so you can quickly find specific topics.

Navigation:

  • Up/Down arrows: Move through the lesson list
  • Enter: Open a lesson's detail view to read its content
  • Tab: Switch between Active Lessons and All Lessons modes
  • Home/End: Jump to first or last lesson
  • Type letters: Typeahead search (in All Lessons mode)
  • Backspace: Delete search character
  • Escape: Clear search, or close the menu

Inside a lesson's detail view:

  • Up/Down: Navigate through the lesson header, help text lines, and action buttons
  • Enter: Activate the current button (e.g., "Mark as learned")
  • Escape: Return to the lesson list

Each lesson shows its knowledge percentage (how much the game considers you've learned it). Arrowing through a lesson's detail view counts as interaction and increases your knowledge. You can also press Enter on "Mark as learned" to immediately complete a lesson.

Note: The Learning Helper requires adaptive training to be enabled in your settings. If adaptive training is off, the ? key will do nothing.

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• Fixed auto slaughter typeahead not working: typing letters on the auto slaughter screen was navigating the animals menu instead. Typeahead now correctly searches animal rows on the auto slaughter screen.
  • Fixed AZERTY keyboard support: the left ALT key should now work for all ALT shortcuts (Alt+N, Alt+H, Alt+M, Alt+B, etc.). Previously, only the right ALT key worked on AZERTY and similar non-US keyboard layouts.
  • Fixed keyboard input leaking from the health tab operations menu: typing letters for typeahead search (e.g., 'R' or 'T') was accidentally triggering game shortcuts (drafting pawns, announcing time). Letters are now properly consumed by the menu.
  • Added Enter-to-confirm-search behavior across tabular menus: in the auto slaughter, animals, and wildlife menus, pressing Enter while a typeahead search is active now confirms the search result and announces your current position, instead of triggering the cell action. Press Enter again (after search is cleared) to interact with the cell normally.
  • Fixed IMGUI focus on character creation pages after closing the faction relations dialog

Massive character creation overhaul, full Ideology DLC browsing, Odyssey gravship support, Royalty jump pack targeting, localization of 70+ hardcoded strings, and a new pawn filter system with RandomPlus compatibility.

Important Note: Creating custom ideoligions is not yet accessible. Do not select those options in the ideology screen or you will get stuck and have to restart the game. Support for this will come in a few days to a week.

docs.title: CHARACTER CREATION — REDESIGNED
docs.text:
The character creation screen has been completely rebuilt as a treeview. Pawns are grouped under "Selected" and "Left behind" headers, with expandable categories (Bio, Traits, Skills, Health, Possessions) and full keyboard navigation.

  • Page Up/Down preserves your tree position when switching between pawns
  • Ctrl+Up/Down reorders pawns within the selected group
  • Alt+R randomizes the current pawn
  • Alt+N renames with a Title field
  • Right bracket (]) opens a context menu with Biotech dev stage and xenotype submenus
  • Typeahead search to find pawns by name
  • Start-game confirmation now lists pawn names

Xenotype editor (Biotech DLC): The gene editing screen during character creation is now fully accessible. Tabbed treeview with Selected Genes, Gene Library (organized by category), and Controls (biostats, name, name lock, inheritable, ignore restrictions, load/save). Toggle individual genes with Enter, rename with a text input flow, and browse gene details with front-loaded biostats and descriptions.

Pawn filter system (RandomPlus Mod implementation) (Alt+F or context menu): A full pawn filter editor lets you set criteria for auto-rerolling pawns. Filters include per-skill level and passion requirements, total passion range, total skill points range, traits (required/excluded), age range, gender, health conditions, and work incapabilities. When randomizing, pawns are rerolled automatically until a match is found or the configurable limit is reached, with progress announcements for long searches.

RandomPlus feature parity: The filter system now matches the full RandomPlus mod feature set — gene-affected hediff exemptions, optional trait pools, skill counting options (highest attack only, passion skills only), and reroll limits up to 50,000. Filter presets save and load in the exact same format and location as RandomPlus, so blind and sighted players can share presets seamlessly.

docs.title: WANDERER DIALOG
docs.text: The post-colony-death settler creation screen (Dialog_ChooseNewWanderers) is now fully accessible, reusing the same chargen tree navigation and RandomPlus filter system. Alt+A to add pawns (up to 6), Delete to remove (minimum 1), Enter to confirm, Escape to close. The pawn filter and reroll work mid-game just like during initial character creation.

docs.title: LOCALIZATION
docs.text:
Over 70 hardcoded English strings across the main menu, options menu, storyteller selection, scenario selection, and custom difficulty screens have been replaced with RimWorld's own translation keys. Tooltip announcements have been added for 14 settings that have game-provided tooltips (volumes, compression, camera, etc.).

The language selection menu and soundtrack submenu now route through the accessible float menu system instead of opening vanilla's inaccessible FloatMenu. Language names display in their native script (e.g., "Deutsch" instead of "German").

On/Off checkbox values, day labels, permadeath mode labels, and option category names are all localized.

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• Map cursor now initializes at the camera position instead of (0,0) when loading a save
  • Fixed a crash when the game's rendering code called TransportersInGroup() during gizmo announcement, causing a collection-modified exception
  • Fixed incompatible trait degrees (e.g., Psychically Hypersensitive and Psychically Deaf) being selectable together in the pawn filter
  • Fixed float menu input conflicts with IMGUI context on chargen pages
  • Fixed favorite color translation crash due to missing named arguments
  • Ideology tree expand/collapse actions now announce just the section name and state (e.g., "Memes, expanded, 3 items") instead of reading the full content

docs.title: IDEOLOGY DLC
docs.text:
Ideology tab (F12 > Ideology): The in-game Ideology tab is now fully browsable with keyboard navigation. A two-panel interface shows the ideology list on one side and a details tree view on the other.

The details tree includes all sections matching what sighted players see:

  • Overview with leader title, worship room, adjective, member name
  • Style categories with buildable/styled item lists and override tracking
  • Memes as expandable nodes showing unlocked roles, rituals, traits, research, and conflicting precepts
  • Precepts, roles, rituals, buildings, relics, weapons, animals, apparel
  • Role required apparel with descriptions and Alt+I info cards
  • Deities with name, type, gender, and related meme
  • Fluid ideology development points

Note: Reforming fluid ideoligions is not accessible yet, nor is creating custom fluid or fixed ideoligions. This is coming soon.

  • Appearance section with browsable hair, beard, and tattoo styles
  • Ritual ambience sound preview via Enter key

Ideology preset selection during world gen: The ideology selection screen during world generation is now accessible. Two-tab interface with Options (Classic, Custom Fluid/Fixed, Load) and Presets (organized by Mild/Strong/Intense categories with expandable descriptions). Alt+S and Alt+Y open structure and style selection menus.

Favorite color: Pawn favorite colors now appear in both the info card Bio tab and the inspect treeview Character section.

docs.title: ROYALTY DLC
docs.text: Jump pack targeting: Jump Packs and Locust Armor jump abilities are now fully accessible. When entering jump targeting mode, you hear the ability name, range, and remaining charges. Each tile shows validity as you navigate, R provides detailed range info, and Enter gives specific error messages for invalid targets. This required special handling because Verb_Jump extends Verb directly rather than going through the ability system.

docs.title: ODYSSEY DLC
docs.text:
Gravship support: Gravships (Odyssey DLC flying transports) are now fully accessible, including destination selection, landing placement with coordinate correction, layer cycling on the world map, and disconnected substructure detection with scanner integration.

The process of launching and landing gravships is heavily gizmo driven. Check gizmos (g key) for every gravship related object to learn how the system works.

  • Fixed gravship checkboxes being incorrectly counted in ritual role assignments

Permits are now fully usable from the keyboard, the scanner splits mechanoids into friendly and hostile, thing filter navigation gets several fixes, and a soft-lock with child growth moments is resolved.

docs.title: PERMITS
docs.text:
Permits can now be accepted and returned directly from the Info Card's Permits tab. Each permit node shows its full details — title requirement, prerequisites, cooldown, favor cost, and description. Use Enter to accept an available permit, and "Return all permits" is available per faction with a confirmation prompt.

Permit targeting has also been fixed. Previously, using a permit that targets a map cell (e.g., calling a shuttle or an airstrike) was completely broken because the item targeting system was incorrectly intercepting permit workers. The permit name is now announced when targeting starts, and range validation accounts for weather conditions correctly — clear weather no longer blocks targeting due to a negative range cap.

docs.title: SCANNER
docs.text: • The Mechanoids scanner subcategory is now split into "Player mechanoids" and "Hostile mechanoids" so you can cycle through your own mechs without stopping on every hostile cluster

docs.title: FILTER NAVIGATION (used with ingredient filters, stockpile zone filters, etc.)
docs.text:
• Pressing * (Shift+8 or numpad multiply) now expands all siblings at the current level, matching the standard tree view pattern used elsewhere in the mod
  • Typeahead search now works in the policy editor's ThingFilter (outfit, drug, and food restriction editors)
  • Fixed typeahead keys leaking through to game shortcuts — for example, pressing T to search would also trigger the time announcement

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text: • Fixed a soft-lock in the growth moment dialog when a child turning 3 had no passion or trait choices available — the dialog would open but couldn't be dismissed

Minor hotfix patch.

  • Fixed ingredient filters (e.g., crematorium bills) not showing inherited special filters like "Allow rotten" and "Allow fresh"
  • Colonist bar no longer announces "Start of bar" / "End of bar" when reaching boundaries — instead re-announces the current pawn

Another big patch! The schedule menu assign menu have all been redesigned from scratch, column painting now works across every supported table in the mod, and there are a ton of bug fixes and quality-of-life improvements throughout.

docs.title: MAP AND TILE INFORMATION
docs.text:
The way items on a map tile are reported has been completely overhauled. Previously, items were broken into separate categories (pawns, buildings, items, plants) with arbitrary caps — for example, only the first 2 buildings and 3-5 pawns would be announced, and plants were hidden whenever any other object was present.

Now, everything on a tile is announced with no truncation, sorted by the game's own AltitudeLayer priority system — the same system the game uses for visual rendering and click selection. Higher-priority things are announced first:

  1. Blueprints (planned construction) 2. Pawns (colonists, animals, NPCs) 3. Items (resources, equipment) 4. Buildings (structures, furniture, doors) 5. Plants (trees, crops, wild plants) 6. Conduits (hidden infrastructure)

Player-placed orders (chop, mine, haul, etc.) are now announced alongside the thing they apply to — for example, "bamboo tree (chop wood)" — instead of appearing as a disconnected list at the end. Cell-targeted orders like mine or smooth floor are announced at the beginning since they apply to the tile as a whole.

This same ordering is now used consistently across tile info, Alt+I info cards, and the gizmo bar, so all three systems present things in the same order.

Other tile info changes:

  • Polluted terrain now includes "Polluted" in the label, matching vanilla's display
  • Alt+I can now inspect non-selectable things like filth and wild plants

docs.title: SCHEDULE MENU (F2) — REDESIGNED
docs.text:
The schedule menu has been completely redesigned. It now uses a brush- based painting system that lets you assign jobs across hours quickly using keyboard shortcuts.

How it works: The schedule is a grid where each row is a pawn and each column is an hour of the day (0–23). Each cell can be set to a job type like Anything, Work, Sleep, Recreation, or Meditate (if you have the Royalty DLC).

Selecting a brush: Press number keys 1 through 4 (or 5 with Royalty) to select a brush. The brushes correspond to the available job types: 1 = Anything 2 = Work (if available) 3 = Sleep 4 = Recreation 5 = Meditate (Royalty DLC) The selected brush is announced when you pick it.

Applying the brush:

  • Space or Enter: Apply the brush to the current cell
  • Shift+Left/Right: Move to the next/previous hour AND apply the brush as you go — this is "painting." Hold Shift and arrow across hours to quickly set a range.
  • Shift+Home/End: Paint from the current cell to the first/last hour of the row
  • Ctrl+Shift+Home/End: Paint every row at the selected column with the active brush.

For example: Let's say you have three pawns, Bob, Alice and John:

It's currently 11:43 in the game, and they're all having a really difficulty day, so you want to allow them to have recreation time the next two hours. You'd press f2, hit the right arrow key once (to navigate to hour 12 then press 3 to select the recreation brush.

From here, you could do a few different things:

  1. You could press space on hour 12 to paint that single tile with your recreation brush. 2. You could tap shift right arrow, to select both hours 12 and 1 with your recreation brush (for your first pawn.) 3. Or, you could press control shift end. This would paint hour 12 with your recreation brush for all three of your pawns. Then you'd just have to hit the right arrow key to select hour 13 and use control shift home to paint all three pawns with recreation for hour 13.

If you'd rather just use] space to set individual cells, that's perfectly fine too. You can also still use control c and control v to copy and paste schedules between pawns.

If this proves to be confusing for folks (I'm assuming it will) I can make a video about it if Liam doesn't! I also will be updating the README to describe this screen in more detail.

Feedback is always welcome!

Navigation:

  • Up/Down arrows move between pawns
  • Left/Right arrows move between hours
  • Tab/Shift+Tab switches between Schedule and Allowed Areas columns
  • Home/End jump to the first/last hour
  • Typeahead search to find pawns by name

docs.title: ASSIGN MENU (F3) — REDESIGNED
docs.text:
The assign menu has been completely rebuilt to match the game's actual table layout — the same column-based design used by the Animals and Wildlife menus. Each row is a pawn and each column is an assignment category (Outfit, Drug Policy, Food Restriction, Hostility Response, Medical Care, Allowed Area, etc.).

  • Left/Right arrows move between columns
  • Up/Down arrows move between pawns
  • Enter or Space opens a submenu for the current column (e.g., a list of available outfit policies to choose from)
  • Right bracket (]) opens a context menu with actions for the current cell
  • Typeahead search to find pawns by name

Painting is fully supported (see Column Painting below). You can also jump directly into the policy editor for outfits, food, and drugs from within the assign menu, and when you close the editor, you're returned to where you left off.

docs.title: COLUMN PAINTING (Animals, Wildlife, Assign, Schedule)
docs.text:
"Painting" is a new way to apply the same value across multiple rows in a column without having to change each cell individually. Think of it like drag-to-fill in a spreadsheet. This feature previously existed only when setting allowed areas. It now works across every supported column in the Animals, Wildlife, and Assign tabs as well.

How painting works: 1. Navigate to the cell whose value you want to copy 2. Hold Shift and press Down or Up to paint that value to the next or previous row 3. Keep holding Shift and arrowing to keep painting

Bulk painting shortcuts: Since only the schedule tab lets you paint in the horizontal direction, all other tables will happily let you bulk paint whether you use shift home and shift end, or control shift home and control shift end.

Paintable columns by tab:

Animals (F4):

  • Training columns (Obedience, Release, Rescue, Haul, etc.)
  • Checkbox columns (Slaughter, Sterile, Follow Drafted, Follow Fieldwork, Release to Wild, plus Odyssey columns like Animal Dig and Animal Forage)
  • Master assignment
  • Medical Care level
  • Allowed Area

Wildlife (F5):

  • Hunt and Tame checkboxes

Assign (F3):

  • Outfit, Drug Policy, Food Restriction, Hostility Response, Medical Care, and other assignment columns

Schedule (F2):

  • All hour cells (using the brush system described above)

Animals and cells that can't accept the value (e.g., an animal that can't learn a training skill) are automatically skipped. Each column type plays appropriate sound effects matching vanilla's behavior.

docs.title: WORK MENU IMPROVEMENTS
docs.text:
• Shift+0 through Shift+4: Set the selected work type's priority for ALL compatible pawns at once. The announcement adapts based on how many were changed vs. how many are incapable of that work type.
  • Tab/Shift+Tab now preserves your work type column when moving between pawns, so you can quickly compare the same job across all colonists (e.g., Tab through every pawn's Cooking priority without losing your column position).

docs.title: INVENTORY IMPROVEMENTS
docs.text:
Consolidated item groups: All instances of the same item type (same material and quality) are now grouped under a single expandable parent node showing the total count and how many are being carried. Expand the group to see individual stacks with their storage locations (stockpile zone, shelf, building) or carrier pawn, plus forbidden and tainted indicators.

Material variant grouping: Items with multiple material or quality variants (apparel, weapons, furniture) are further grouped by their base type. For example, all parkas are grouped together under "Parka" regardless of material, with a summary showing total count and materials. Meal variants sharing the same tier (fine, lavish) are grouped by quality.

Context menus: Press right bracket (]) on any item to open a context menu with actions like Jump To, Drop, Install, and Show Info, with keyboard shortcut hints shown alongside each action.

docs.title: BILL CONFIGURATION FIXES
docs.text:
• Store In dropdown: Previously only showed stockpile zones, completely missing shelves and shelf groups. Selecting a shelf showed "(No stockpile)". Now correctly lists all storage locations including shelf groups, sorted to match vanilla's ordering. Compatible locations are listed first, with incompatible ones marked.
  • Look In dropdown (ingredient source): Previously showed every storage location as a flat list without grouping shelves that share a storage group. Now properly collapses linked shelves into single group entries.
  • Auto-pause: Bills paused by the "pause when satisfied" feature now show "(Paused)" in the bill list, and the bill config menu gains an "Unpause" option that appears only when a bill is auto-paused.
  • Approximately 40 previously hardcoded English strings have been replaced with the game's own translation keys, improving support for non-English players. Please let me know if the experience was actually made worse for you!

docs.title: POLICY EDITORS (Outfit, Food, Drug)
docs.text:
The three policy editors now share unified keyboard shortcuts that work from both the table view and the dropdown selector:

  • Alt+N: New policy
  • Alt+R: Rename policy
  • Alt+C: Copy policy
  • Alt+E: Edit policy (opens filter)
  • Delete: Delete policy

Context menu labels now show these shortcut hints.

Item filter improvements across all policy editors, storage filters, and bill ingredient filters:

  • Categories now use tri-state toggling matching vanilla behavior. When a category is partially allowed (some items on, some off), toggling it turns everything ON instead of OFF.
  • Smart category summaries now show exception counts and names instead of a misleading "allowed" or "disallowed" label. For example, "disallowed, except for: cloth, human leather."
  • Navigation in subcategories should no longer get stuck when drilling into and out of nested filter trees.
  • Asterisk prefixes on special filter labels are stripped for cleaner screen reader output.

Other policy editor fixes:

  • Forced apparel is now listed in the outfit column values on the assign tab
  • Closing a policy editor properly returns to the assign menu and re-announces your position

docs.title: GIZMO BAR AND ORDERS
docs.text:
Reverse designator gizmos: Orders like Mine Vein, Strip Corpse, and other reverse designators are now accessible in the gizmo menu (G key) when you have a valid target selected. Mine Vein, for example, lets you place a mine order on an entire connected body of mineable tiles — select any tile in the vein, press G to open gizmos, and activate Mine Vein to mark the whole thing.

Ability cooldowns: Ability gizmos now announce their cooldown remaining when on cooldown, so you can tell when an ability will be available again.

Queued orders: When you give an order with Shift+Enter (to queue it rather than replace the current order), the announcement now confirms that the order was queued.

docs.title: INFO CARDS AND INSPECTION
docs.text:
• Ctrl+Alt+I: New shortcut to open the info card for the currently selected colonist bar pawn, matching the existing Ctrl+Alt+Enter pattern for the inspection tree.
  • Incapable Of section: The info card's "Incapable Of" section now shows WHY each work type is disabled (which backstory, trait, or gene causes it) and expands to list affected work types with descriptions, matching what sighted players see on the character card.

docs.title: KEYBOARD AND INPUT FIXES
docs.text:
• Shift+Home/End on sliders: The direction of Shift+Home and Shift+End has been corrected across all quantity sliders (caravans, trading, bills, auto-slaughter, difficulty, fishing zones, quantity menu). Home now goes to minimum and End goes to maximum, matching standard keyboard conventions.
  • Building mode no longer steals Escape when an overlay screen (inventory, gizmo navigation, inspection) is open on top of it. Previously, pressing Escape while viewing inventory during placement mode could discard your blueprint instead of closing the inventory.

docs.title: AUTO-SLAUGHTER UX IMPROVEMENTS
docs.text:
• Tab/Shift+Tab now cycles between the Animals menu and Auto Slaughter screen, with Escape closing both screens entirely.
  • Typing -1 in numeric input now sets the value to unlimited.

docs.title: BIOTECH DLC
docs.text:
Gene inspection for items: Embryos, genepacks, and xenogerms now have full gene inspection support. Previously, inspecting these items showed "Category not found." Now you can browse their gene lists in the inspection tree and see skin color shade descriptions (very light, light, fair, medium, etc.) in both overview and info card views.

Soft-lock fix: Fixed a soft-lock that occurred when baby naming or growth moment dialogs were force-opened by the game's timer (when the associated letter times out). Keyboard navigation would partially work but Enter and Escape failed, trapping blind players. Both dialog types now initialize correctly regardless of how they're opened.
There's a lot of stuff in here, and it's not as organized as I would like, but just about every change should be documented!

docs.title: COLONIST BAR NAVIGATION
docs.text:
Full keyboard navigation for the colonist bar, giving you quick access to any pawn without having to hit comma and period a million times.

  • Alt+Left/Right navigates the bar linearly across page boundaries
  • Alt+Up/Down moves between pages of 10 (colonist pages, then mechs)
  • Alt+1-0 jumps to positions on the current page
  • Ctrl+Alt+Left/Right reorders colonists within a page
  • Ctrl+Alt+Up/Down moves colonists between pages
  • Reorder announcements include neighbor context (e.g., "between X and Y")
  • Ctrl+Alt+Enter opens the inspection tree for the selected colonist
  • Comma/Period cycles through mechs when on the mech section. (Repositioning mechs on mech bar is coming soon, but it will take more time, because in Vanilla Rimworld, there is no such thing as a mech bar.)

docs.title: COVER INFO
docs.text:
Drafted and hostile pawns now announce their cover status across the map cursor, scanner, and colonist bar (Comma/Period, Alt+number). Shows the best adjacent cover object and its base block chance percentage, e.g., "behind sandbags (blocks 55%)".

Note: reported percentages reflect the object's base block chance and may not match actual combat effectiveness, which varies based on shooter angle, distance, and diagonal positioning.

docs.title: QUEST SYSTEM
docs.text:
The quest list now announces full quest info (name, difficulty, time limit, description, and rewards) when arrowing through entries, and you can press enter to drill into and arrow through details.

  • Alt+A on multi-choice reward quests opens a menu for selecting between reward options
  • Alt+I within that menu opens a nested item inspection sub-menu and Enter opens info cards for individual items
  • Escape navigates back through each level
  • Accept buttons in detail view now show reward descriptions
  • Opening hint explains Alt+A, Alt+D, and Enter navigation on first open
  • You can now choose which pawn will accept a quest for quests which require a specific pawn to accept them.
  • When in the quest menu, you can press tab to configure desired goodwill / honor quest rewards per faction for future quests.

docs.title: FACTIONS TAB (F12)
docs.text:
The in-game Factions tab is now accessible. Press F12 to open it (also works for the Ideology tab if that DLC is active). Though the ideology tab is not accessible just yet!

Each faction is a collapsible treeview node. Expanding reveals individual sections: type, leader, relations, goodwill with ongoing/recent event breakdown, ideology, enemies, and description. The description itself is expandable into individual lines for easier parsing.

  • Typeahead search to find factions by name
  • Alt+I for info cards on factions
  • Standard WCAG treeview keyboard shortcuts (Right/Left expand/collapse, Home/End siblings, Ctrl+Home/End absolute, * expand all siblings)
  • The pre-game faction landing page (F key during starting site selection) uses the same treeview navigation

This is a bit of an experiment. All the information is shown as you arrow through each faction, but you can optionally hit the right arrow key (since this is a tree view,) and arrow through the information if you want to receive the information in chunks. Annoyingly, when you do hit the right arrow key to expand the item, it will read the full text of the item again, so hit the down arrow key immediately after expanding. If people like this, I will add this functionality to other tree views throughout the mod, and I'll make it not announce long menu items when expanding / collapsing them.

docs.title: BILL CONFIGURATION OVERHAUL
docs.text:
The bill configuration screen now has full feature parity with the vanilla Dialog_BillConfig, adding a bunch of previously missing options:

  • Rename bills
  • Include equipped / include tainted toggles
  • Currently-have count display
  • HP range and quality range filters
  • Limit to allowed stuff
  • Include from source stockpile selection
  • Independent skill range min/max controls
  • Ingredient search radius editing
  • Recipe descriptions shown in bill config info
  • Skill requirements now show actual minimums instead of learn factor
  • Work amounts use the game's native formatting
  • Home/End keys for bill config navigation
  • DLC-specific options: slave/mech/non-mech workers (Biotech/Ideology), style selection (Ideology), wearable-by info (Biotech)

docs.title: AUTO-SLAUGHTER OVERHAUL
docs.text:
The auto-slaughter settings screen has been completely rewritten with a clearer, more accessible interface.

New features:

  • Inline quantity shortcuts: Shift+Up/Down (±10), Ctrl+Up/Down (±100)
  • Direct number typing: Enter to activate, type digits, Enter to confirm
  • Natural language announcements with descriptive column names (e.g., "Maximum allowed males: 5. Current population: 3")
  • Slaughter preview per column ("3 will be slaughtered")
  • Slaughter summary on close listing all animals marked across species
  • Smart unlimited-to-limit transition: pressing + sets to current count + 1, pressing - sets to current count - 1
  • Shift+Home sets column to unlimited, Shift+End sets to 0

Bug fixes from the original implementation:

  • Counting logic now matches vanilla exactly: bonded animals excluded from category counts when bonded slaughter is disabled; pregnant females excluded from female/total counts when pregnant slaughter is disabled
  • Pressing + at unlimited no longer incorrectly sets limit to 0

docs.title: PEN MARKER / ANIMAL PENS
docs.text:
Pen marker accessibility has been aligned with the vanilla implementation:

  • Pen animal filter now correctly shows only roamer animals instead of every animal in the game (same fix applied to storage and bill ingredient filters)
  • Auto-Cut expanded from a single action to a menu with toggle, Cut Now button, and plant filter
  • Pen Food now shows unenclosed check, pen size, stockpile duration, and example animals with live add/remove
  • Pen markers can be renamed

Note: I meant to add pens to the scanner with their names, but I forgot. They'll be included in either my next test patch or my PR, whichever comes first.

docs.title: BUILDING AND PLACEMENT
docs.text:
• Shift+R rotates buildings counter-clockwise during placement (R still rotates clockwise)
  • In-progress buildings, unfinished crafted items, fermenting barrels, and gene assemblers now announce work remaining
  • Buildings with multiple interaction cells (e.g., school desks with student/teacher spots) are now announced during placement and cursor navigation
  • Facility linking is now accessible: placement announcements show facility bonuses and distance constraints, and a new "Linked Facilities" category in the inspection tree shows linked buildings, active/inactive status, compatible facilities, and stat bonuses. Applies to blackboards, tool cabinets, end tables, dressers, vitals monitors, and similar buildings
  • Generic building owner assignment now works for any assignable building (meditation spots, thrones, graves, etc.), not just beds
  • Meditation focus info tree node shows nearby focus objects with type, strength, distance, and line-of-sight info
  • Building placement is blocked in meditation focus protection zones when the warning toggle gizmo is enabled, with announcements guiding you to disable it if needed

docs.title: AREA ASSIGNMENT (Alt+A)
docs.text: Press Alt+A on the colony map to quickly assign an allowed area to the pawn at cursor or selected pawn. Includes Manage Areas integration and typeahead search. This is the only way to set assigned areas for friendly mechs.

docs.title: SCANNER
docs.text: • Press Ctrl+Z to clear the scanner search filter

docs.title: SOUND EFFECTS
docs.text: The windowless float menu (right-click context menus) now plays the correct game sounds: FloatMenu_Open when opening, ColonistOrdered when executing an order, ClickReject for disabled options, and FloatMenu_Cancel when dismissing.

docs.title: SPEECH AND KEYBOARD
docs.text:
• All screen reader output now passes through a centralized sanitization pipeline that automatically strips XML/color tags, fixes double periods and bad punctuation, and collapses extra whitespace
  • AZERTY keyboard support: the asterisk key (* for expand all siblings in treeviews) now works on AZERTY and other non-US layouts where Unity reports the key differently

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• Designators (e.g., mine orders) are now announced on fog-of-war tiles instead of being silently skipped
  • Fixed keyboard input being consumed by world navigation when a dialog box appeared during starting site selection (e.g., pollution warnings)
  • Fixed starting site selection state sync issues on initial Enter press
  • Fixed site selection re-announcing the tile instead of confirming your choice
  • Suppressed redundant site selection announcement when advancing to the next page
  • Fixed IMGUI focus loss after opening the faction relations dialog during character creation, which caused complete keyboard unresponsiveness on subsequent pages
  • Escape now properly navigates back from the pawn selection screen
  • Fixed Alt+number keys conflicting with tile info and time control hotkeys (Alt+number now always targets the colonist bar)

docs.title: BIOTECH DLC
docs.text:
Xenogerm creation (gene processor):

  • Full keyboard accessibility for the gene assembler dialog
  • Tabbed treeview: Library, Selected Genepacks, and Controls
  • tree view navigation for genepacks with expandable gene details
  • Enter to add/remove genepacks, biostats updated live
  • Controls tab: biostats, rename, name lock, randomize, save template, load template, start combining, close
  • Save/Load xenotype templates

Growth moments (ages 7, 10, 13):

  • Full keyboard accessibility for the child growth moment dialog
  • Tabbed navigation for info, passions, and traits
  • Growth tier gizmo now announces points, learning rate, next growth moment age, and tier reward details

Learning desires:

  • Active learning desires for children are now shown beneath the Learning need in both the Alt+N quick needs readout and the inspect treeview

Mechanitor control groups:

  • Two-page interface for mech control groups
  • Settings page: work mode, recharge range, select all
  • Members page: energy levels, reassignment between groups
  • Rich gizmo labels and status in the gizmo bar

docs.title: ROYALTY DLC
docs.text:
Meditation focus:

  • Building inspection now includes a meditation focus tree node showing nearby focus objects with type, strength, distance, and line-of-sight
  • Building placement respects meditation focus protection zones when the warning toggle is enabled

docs.title: GAME SETUP OVERHAUL
docs.text:
Parts of the character creation process have been cleaned up and modernized a little. This process is not yet complete!

  • Difficulty selection screen now properly supports home / end, typeahead, etc. Additionally, commitment mode is now a list with two items, rather than a weird checkbox.
  • Custom difficulty settings can be browsed and edited directly
  • World generation screen redesigned for keyboard navigation, with the same controls now used for both world gen and in-game world map views
  • Faction configuration screen (where you choose which factions appear in your game) is now keyboard accessible. Press tab while configuring world generation settings to access.
  • Faction landing page (the screen shown while selecting your landing site) is now accessible by pressing 'f'.
  • You can now view faction relations during starting site selection
  • The scenario selection screen now announces helpful hints when it opens (Tab to switch panels, Alt+E to edit)
  • The world generation settings screen now supports all of the settings available to sighted players, and the sliders mirror the range a sighted player would have. Previously, each slider only had 3 possible states. Now, most have 7.

docs.title: OPERATIONS LIST
docs.text: The operations list (health tab, Operations) has been rebuilt with typeahead search and filtering. Start typing to filter the list by name. Additionally, available operations now match those which the game shows a sighted player, rather than all in existence.

docs.title: ITEM TARGETING
docs.text: Items with "use on target" abilities (like sentience catalysts, and similar targetable items) now work with the accessibility cursor. When you activate one, it enters targeting mode just like abilities do.

docs.title: SCANNER
docs.text: • Scanner performance has been significantly improved, so PageUp/PageDown navigation should feel snappier on maps with lots of objects

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• Fixed a long-standing crash/freeze that could happen when reloading a save while in-game
  • Fixed world map showing fragmented biome regions instead of clean boundaries if you owned the Odyssey DLC
  • Right bracket key should now work on non-US keyboard layouts (e.g., German)
  • Scanner now correctly jumps to bulk groups with or without auto jump mode being enabled.
  • Scanner bulk group jump no longer gets stuck or blocked by placement mode
  • Tile announcements with designators no longer repeat the thing name (e.g., "wooden wall, deconstruct" instead of "wooden wall, wooden wall, deconstruct")

docs.title: INFO CARDS EVERYWHERE (Alt+I)
docs.text:
The biggest addition in this patch for Vanilla Rimworld: you can now press Alt+I in nearly any menu or screen to open the info card for whatever you have selected. Info cards are the detailed stat sheets that sighted players access by clicking the (i) button -- and until now, screen reader users had few ways to reach them. They're now available in 15 different contexts:

  • Map cursor (when hovering over buildings, items, terrain, or pawns)
  • Architect menu (get stats on a building before you place it)
  • Plant selection menu
  • Storage settings (check details on any item in the filter list)
  • Bills menu and bill configuration
  • Gizmo bar (abilities, build commands, and more)
  • Colony inventory
  • Research menu and research detail view (inspect unlocked items and recipes)
  • Colony animals menu
  • Wildlife menu
  • Float menus (right-click context menus)
  • Pawn inspection: gear, health conditions, and genes all support Alt+I
  • Inside info cards themselves -- follow hyperlinks to drill into related entries

Some items (especially within info cards) that have an info card available will say "Inspectable" when you navigate to them, so you always know when Alt+I will work. I want to extend this across the entire mod, but right now, things that are very clearly items / buildings / plants don't say this since it should be assumed that you can press alt i.

Nested info card navigation:

  • When an info card mentions another item (like a material or a research project), you can press Alt+I again to open that item's info card
  • Press Escape to go back to the previous card -- your cursor position is remembered
  • When a stat entry links to multiple items, a selection menu appears so you can choose which one to inspect

Stat entries that can be expanded now correctly detect whether they actually have explanation text, so you won't see "No items to show" on entries that have nothing to expand.

docs.title: PAWN SKILLS SHORTCUT (Alt+K)
docs.text: Press Alt+K while a pawn is selected to hear their top 3 skills along with passion levels. A quick way to check what a pawn is good at without opening the full character sheet.

docs.title: ABILITIES AND TARGETING
docs.text:
Full keyboard-accessible targeting for abilities. This covers all ability types automatically, possibly including modded ones.

Targeting mode:

  • Announces ability name, range, and effect radius
  • Press R to check distance to cursor and line of sight status
  • Press T to hear which pawns are in the area of effect (AOE abilities)
  • Clear error messages for out of range, blocked line of sight, and missing targets
  • Supports two-phase abilities like Skip (select target, then destination)
  • Self-cast abilities announce "Casting [name]" for confirmation
  • Touch-range abilities correctly announce "Touch range"

Ability gizmo announcements:

  • Gizmos now announce their description, range, and effect radius when browsing

docs.title: WILDLIFE MENU OVERHAUL
docs.text:
The wildlife menu has been redesigned to match what sighted players see:

  • Predators are now clearly marked and sorted to the top of the list
  • Columns now match the vanilla game: Manhunter on Damage and Manhunter on Tame Fail replace the old mod-added columns (Age, BodySize, Health, Pregnant)
  • Column tooltips are announced when you move left/right between columns (but not when scrolling up/down through animals, so they don't get repetitive)
  • Hunt and Tame columns now say "Yes" or "No" instead of showing blank text
  • Press Enter on an animal's name to jump the map cursor directly to it

docs.title: TOGGLE GIZMO DESCRIPTIONS
docs.text: Toggle buttons on the gizmo bar (like "Animals attack: ON") now include their tooltip description, giving you the same context that sighted players get on hover. For example: "Animals attack: OFF. While this is on, mastered animals are sent forth to attack distant targets. While it is off, they remain near and guard the master."

docs.title: PAWN INFORMATION IMPROVEMENTS
docs.text:
• Health capacity tooltips now show what's actually affecting the capacity (which hediffs, body parts, or genes are involved) instead of a generic description
  • Skill passion indicators now say "Minor passion" and "Major passion" instead of * and **

docs.title: TERRAIN AND MAP INFO
docs.text:
• Terrain fertility is now included in the tile info announcement (key 2), shown right after the terrain name. Example: "Rich soil (140% fertility)"
  • Light info (key 4) now shows the light level as a percentage, matching what sighted players see

docs.title: MAP AND SCANNER
docs.text:
• Doors now announce whether they're open or closed
  • Example: "wooden door (open)" or "autodoor (closed)"
  • Scanner (PageUp/PageDown) now shows pawn activity
  • Example: "cooking four lavish meals" or "sleeping"
  • Uses your existing ShowPawnActivityOnMap setting

docs.title: COMMS CONSOLE
docs.text: • Dialog navigation now works correctly when using the comms console. Selecting options that lead to sub-menus (like choosing a trader type) takes you to the sub-menu instead of closing the dialog.

docs.title: BUG FIXES
docs.text:
• Fixed double periods appearing in some gizmo announcements
  • Fixed rich text tags appearing in letter and message announcements (no more "(*Name)Bob(/Name)" -- now just shows "Bob")
  • Zone rename no longer breaks in non-English translations
  • Drafting/undrafting with R now plays the same sound as the UI button
  • Targeting now correctly uses the accessibility cursor position instead of the mouse position

docs.title: ROYALTY DLC
docs.text:
Psycast targeting:

  • Announces psyfocus cost and neural heat when targeting psycasts
  • Clear messages for psychic immunity
  • Works on the world map for abilities like Farskip

Psycast gizmo announcements:

  • Psycast gizmos announce their costs when browsing. Example: "Vertigo pulse. Costs 2% psyfocus, requires 50%. Neural heat: 30. [description]. Range: 25. (M)"

Neural heat gizmo:

  • Shows limiter state: "Neural heat: 0/80, Psyfocus: 39%, Limiter: ON"
  • Press Enter on the gizmo to toggle the neural heat limiter

Permits overhaul:

  • The permits screen now shows all available permits for each faction, matching what sighted players see
  • Each permit shows its actual status: Granted, Granted (on cooldown), Available (with how many points you have), or Locked (with what title or prerequisite you need)
  • Your current title, unused permit points, and royal favor are shown per faction
  • Expand a permit to see its required title

docs.title: IDEOLOGY DLC
docs.text:
Role management on the Social tab:

  • The Ideology & Role section now lets you browse all available roles for your ideo
  • Each role shows its current holder (or "No role assigned")
  • Expand a role to see its description, requirements, and effects
  • Assign or unassign roles directly from the inspection tree -- if a pawn isn't eligible, it tells you why

Certainty is now displayed with properly translated labels.

Important NOTE: Ideology is still not fully accessible! Mainly, you can't make your own ideoligion until I've finished revamping the set up screen. If you want to test these changes, do not save your game after enabling ideology. You will end up with a random ideoligion which can have really... interesting, sometimes disastrous consequences for the relationships of your pawns.

docs.title: BIOTECH DLC
docs.text:
Pregnancy approach:

  • The Social tab's inspection tree now supports the pregnancy approach system. When viewing a romantic partner's details, you'll find a "Pregnancy approach" menu right after the Relationship line. Expand it to choose between the available options (Normal, Avoid Pregnancy, Try for Baby). If pregnancy isn't possible between the two pawns, it tells you why.

Romance target selection:

  • The Social tab now includes a "Try Romance" option. Navigate the list of viable romance targets, hear their success chance percentages, and press Enter to initiate. If the relationship would cause complications, you'll get a warning dialog before anything happens.

Genes tab:

  • The Genes tab in pawn inspection is now accessible. Browse a pawn's gene list with full keyboard navigation, and press Alt+I to open info cards for individual genes.

Skin color descriptions:

  • Skin color genes now use descriptive shade names based on actual color (very light, light, fair, medium, tan, brown, dark brown) instead of the generic "Skin color" label. This applies in both the info card gene list and the unborn baby gene inspection.

docs.title: ODYSSEY DLC
docs.text:
Fishing zones:

  • Fishing zone menu is now fully accessible
  • Navigate repeat mode, target count, minimum population, and fish species
  • Includes tooltips for population and minimum values

Terrain info:

  • Terrain info (key 2) now includes fish species and population when standing on fishable water

Animal attack targeting:

  • Announces range from master when entering targeting mode
  • Press R to check distance and range status
  • Clear error if out of range, and targeting stays open so you can reposition
  • Animal attack range is shown in the gizmo description

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
Everything new in RimWorld Access, newest first.

Older changes (before version 2.0) are in the pre-2.0 changelog archive.

Version 2.0 is a rebuild of RimWorld Access from the ground up.

Screens are far more consistent than they were. The same keys and the same announcement grammar carry across the main menu, world creation, every tab, every dialog, and most third-party mod screens.

You can also always reach a screen's buttons. The game's toolbar is shown on every screen and Tab will eventually carry you to it, so you should no longer get stuck wondering which key moves you forward.

Menus and dialogs are now the game's real windows instead of invisible copies, so they appear on screen exactly as the game draws them. Someone watching can see where your cursor is, and can use the mouse alongside you.

Some popular mods now have dedicated support, and mods without it are covered by a reader that handles most windows on its own.

Also new: text the game only shows under the mouse pointer is now spoken, developer mode is fully accessible if a little clunky, there are five new languages, and an optional mouse mode reads whatever the pointer touches.

Behind the scenes, rebuilding how one screen works went from about three days to about twenty minutes, so screens should improve a lot faster from here.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Many popular mods now have dedicated support. Character Editor got the most work: the whole editor is a proper screen, covering appearance, health, needs, social, inventory, genes and xenotypes, the browsers, presets, and the def editor. Also supported: RimWorld Together, Colony Manager Redux, Vehicle Framework, A RimWorld of Magic, Simple Sidearms, the Vanilla Expanded mods, Hospitality, RimTalk, Interaction Bubbles, Allow Tool, Alpha Memes, Dubs Bad Hygiene, the Progression mods, and anything built on JecsTools, HugsLib, or XML Extensions. The experience may not be as nice as the vanilla game experience, but I've done what I can. I can't play every mod out there, nor do I have the money to fix them all, but tools will be coming soon so mod builders can add accessibility for their own mods. Stay tuned!
  • Mods without dedicated support are now covered by a generic window reader. It makes settings pages, dialogs, and custom windows navigable, and it recognizes every element type RimWorld supports, and a few others too! Page Up and Page Down jump between a page's sections, and disabled controls say why they are disabled. It is always on, and dedicated support simply takes over where something better exists.
  • Inspection tabs added by mods are now readable and usable, on pawns, buildings, items, and zones. Buttons activate, checkboxes toggle, sliders adjust or take a typed value, and text fields edit. Tabs also gained an "Also shown on this tab" section, listing anything the visual tab draws that the accessible version does not.
  • Text the game only shows while the mouse rests on something is now spoken.
